original: my first date was at the cuddle convention on Valentine's Day. The Cuddle Convention is supposed to be a progressive, *non sexual *event, in which people are encouraged to consider the benefits of physical contact outside of a romantic or sexual context. The event was organized so that we were introduced to touching other people by a slew of progressively more intimate activities after we had undergone the incredibly long and tedious instructions on consent. We practiced *saying no *to each other, and my partner is this exercise told me I *wasn't allowed to touch her hair *because she suspected *I *didn't feel comfortable with it. I wasn't sure how this was different from any other example of someone who feels they know better than you telling you how you feel, but whatever, I accepted it and we continued with the exercise. After this, we were told to get into groups of three and to cuddle creatively with the people in these groups. My two partners, Griffin, and this other woman who was wearing a very long velvet medieval-style dress settled on either side of him as we discussed the differences between cuddling that might lead to hooking up versus cuddling that "wasn't sexual at all," though he opted not to give her his phone number since he told me he wouldn't want to hang out with her outside of that setting. After the event, myself, himself, my friend, his friends, and a couple strangers we picked up on the side of the road, held hands on the way to the next event we were all going to - the Valentine's day dance. In a bizarre, movie like scene, all of us cuddlers - made a single line of 6 as we crossed the street, holding hands, on our way to…

At the dance it turned out we were just in time for a poetry competition in which people had to leave their chair to give their vote about who the superior poet was. I refused to leave my chair for either contestant, not wanting to reinforce the unfairness of this type of grading. Griffin ignored me during the performance, touching and flirting with the girl to his left - a petite brunette wearing glasses who seemed kinda nerdy. She was wearing a bright red dress. Throughout the evening you could see his mind was turning, trying to figure a way for him to get the two of us in bed with him together. I wouldn't necessarily have been opposed, not because I was interested in her but it seemed like potentially an interesting experience to navigate what role I might have during that experience. She seemed less interested, eventually leaving him for another boy who Appeared in a motorcycle helmet towards the end of the evening. was ostensibly already her partner. We went upstairs and sat next to each other drinking a cider he'd bought and he ranted about how much power he had and how interested I was in having sex with him, at one point asking me how much I wanted to have sex with him. I had been thinking no such thing and was unclear why he'd gotten that impression to begin with. I told him so and he backtracked a little, seeming embarrassed. He also talked a bit about how he liked the barbarian life style, and how, in some situations, he might act barbaric or barbarous if the situation fit, though circumstantially only, insisting that normally he was civilized. He actually told me about his plan to bed myself and the other girl and for the sake of being unpredictable, I agreed, but first I took a call from my brother who told me a story about two salamanders he'd seen fucking in a cup as a valentines day present. My tone of voice became so different when I conversed with my brother in that we were both familiar and had a lot in common, that I think my date was put off. In any case, we descended the staircase, he asked her whether she wanted to do this, she said no and then we both started dancing with other people. The energy between us had clearly dissipated but, as our plan stated, we left with each other and descended onto a bus going towards his house. When we arrived at his street, I told him I wanted to go home and he asked if it was because I was afraid he would force me to do something I wasn't comfortable with. I told him that was the case and he assured me he would do no such thing so I agreed apprehensively. We got to his house and cuddled on the couch, discussing again the advantages to cuddling outside of a romantic or sexual context. He then carried me over to his room and I insisted that I no longer wanted to have sex with him. We got naked and did not do anything sexual.  In the morning I looked at his extensive lego collection and he made me breakfast. I was unclear about whether and how much I should help him making the breakfast though the bottom line was that I don't know how to successfully fry an egg. After a while I took a phone call from my friend Alessio and told him about a friend I had. Griffin was ignoring me and I went into the other room to continue my conversation and eventually left. I got lost on the way back to my house and was told by Alpha that I should meet him at a meditation event so I went to a cafe and wrote a story about how passive aggressive the waitress at the cafe had been to me.
OTHER VERSION FROM SOMEWHERE ELSE

I met Griffin at a cuddle convention. Before you say: “A cuddle convention?! That sounds uh-may-zing, it wasn’t that great, and I’ll tell you why. At a cuddle convention, the main point is that cuddling can be a platonic activity that has none of the undertones of creepiness and awkwardness. Basically it can be “touch without meaning.” Well. Perhaps cuddling can be that, however, I am here to say that a cuddle convention, put on by a lot of shitty people as a sad excuse for people who don’t have a valentine on valentine’s day, is not the place where this is likely to take place. And the fact of this date’s existence proves my point.

*So*. I’ll start at the beginning. Alpha and I, having just met each other and “moved in” together (we were staying at his friend Sarah’s house, who owns an air b’n’b but was giving us a discount, had decided we weren’t going to stay at home again so he could go to bed at 10 while I talked to my friend’s Adam and Allessio on the phone till about 3. After all, it was Valentine’s day, and we both hypothetically wanted to find love.

We took the bus to the Cuddle Convention, after making fun of this one woman who got on and off with us, before realizing she was going to the same place as us. To make matters worse, when we appeared in political correctness heaven, at the “Consent Conversation” headquarters, Alpha made a joke to a woman standing outside that it was a load of bullshit that didn’t need a whole half an hour. Then we walked into the convention and that lady was standing at the front of the room, speaking.

The chalkboard behind her had a list of polite ways to say “no” to people. Next we all practiced rescinding consent. She tried to make it fun by making up weird cuddle positions (the alligator where one person’s legs open like an alligator’s mouth), but, the fun was pretty much ruined due to Alpha sweating nervously at the back due to his comment, and the fact that she sucked. Afterwards we journeyed the one block to the actual cuddle room and were introduced to the second layer of hell, in which we got to discuss, with the people we were about to be cuddling, what saying no felt like.

Lucky me, my partner was another one of the event’s organizers. We took turns asking if we could touch different parts of people’s bodies and having them say yes or no. I asked if I could touch her hair and she said “no, because I don’t think *you *would be comfortable with that.”

she alone raised her hand and announced to the whole group that she had said no because she didn’t really think *I *wanted to touch her hair - pointing at me so that the whole groups eyes turned to the one - the creepy one who’d asked for what they could not have.

Then we got into groups and pretended to be animal's, crawling like hippos, cuddling like giraffes - how did zebra’s cuddle. I supposed they hoped to evoke the platonicism of cuddling with a cat or dog, as those are the animal's that most people pretended to be. I was a sloth, not moving at all, waiting ro this torture to be over.

And finally. The last round of cuddling. The one we’d all been waiting for. Inadvertently, I’d found the one attractive male among this sea of potential cuddlers, and perhaps he’d done the same, as we slowly gravitated towards each other.  ended up cuddling this one tall boy with a blonde ponytail. Myself and this other woman who told us she was asexual but still liked human contact. Pillow talk was pretty hopping in our little cuddle threesome, what with his trying to hit on me without hitting on her. We discussed how much we enjoyed the idea that one could cuddle platonicly without their being anything sexual about the situation as his hand snaked it’s way slowly to my butt and I moved his hand away gently. After that was the Valentine’s dance, preceded by a sort of barbaric form of slam poetry in which the audience stands up in their chair in order to vote for the poem they liked best. A great idea, the only problem being staring out at a crowd full of seated people if your poem did not do well. I never did like slam poetry so I simply stayed in my seat. In the spirit of the cuddle convention, we all held hands on the way to the valentine’s dance - myself, the tall blonde boy, a girl with straight hair, and alpha who joined us as we left. A little hard to pass a four-person cuddle monster but, as I always say “cuddling trumps passerby traffic”.

For the final round, griffin and i went upstairs and he made a speech about how he had the ability to control people, and at the end he asked how much I wanted to have sex with him. I told him not at all and wandered off to call my brother who told me he had seen two salamander’s making love in an aquarium that day - god’s Valentine’s day gift to the world. We met again downstairs and he told me how much he wanted to bang me and that other chick at the same time. We watched as she danced with another boy who had come to meet her there. Then we went home to cuddle platonically and actually did. In the morning he made me eggs and played a video game while I talked on the phone to my friend Alessio. A few months later I ran into him at a party but I was with another boy and I didn’t want to talk to him. Add the part about him being a barbarian.

original: My date with Jon Storch was the first okcupid date I'd been on in Portland after I'd been messaging a number of guys for the week I'd been in Portland I'd yet to meet up with one. I sent him the first message after we liked each other about where he'd graduated from (Brown) and I told him I was going to an art museum which he chose to meet me at. I put on a funkyish dress with a blue silky top part and an orange and green patterned longish bottom and I put my black high-heeled boots on with it, and I neglected to bring my backpack and I put on my black shoulder-padded jacket. I felt I looked good considering the small amount of time I'd spent getting ready and the lack of intent to look well put together. My hair I put up in a loose knot/bun.

I went to a Japanese restaurant with Alpha right before going to the art museum and ordered raw fish and a Sapporo. When Jon arrived, I was sitting at a table with Alpha, my oldish friend who got up when Jon arrived and made conversation with him for a minute before leaving. Jon appeared uncomfortable while speaking with Alpha. He took Alpha's place in front of me at the table and I offered him food and some beer but he wanted neither and looked somewhat alarmed perhaps he thought I planned for him to pay. He was wearing a hipster sweater, maroon I think, and tight jeans. He was wearing glasses and his face was gaunt and he was skinny. I had spoken to him on the phone while he was on the bus and told him that I was at a Japanese restaurant. We talked about him going to school at Brown, he asked me about Wesleyan, dropping out, we talked about the social dynamics at each of our schools, I mentioned that my fellow students were none to happy with the administration, I suggested that I had somewhat quit because I didn't like school, I made it sound like I didn't like Wesleyan. He told me his problems with the administration at his own school. He told me about certain things their administration had done recently that he and his fellow students were none too pleased about. He said he had worked for the newspaper that published news about things like that. He told me about the resignation of their former president who I had witnessed when I had come to watch my brother graduate from college, but I did not mention my brother having gone to Brown and I did not mention that I knew the president he was talking about nor that I had heard her speak. Apparently the new president was even worse and he and his friends had a lot of problems with the new president.

His speech was somewhat hesitant, somewhat excited/passionate/enthusiastic and he seemed genuinely interested and invested in the topics. He seemed less than confident about talking to me but not necessarily because of me but he seemed somewhat nervous in general. I felt that he must have assumed that I agreed with almost everything he said. I didn't make known any disagreements which I may or may not have had, I was a little unsure about what he was saying and perhaps feigned more knowledge on the subject and of liberalism in general and current events than I had in actuality.

I finished my raw fish and my beer and asked for the check and paid for the check with my debit card which struck me as a funny moment. We left the restaurant and started walking. We decided to go to the library and to see after that if we wanted to go the art museum. He said he worked in a church nearby. He seemed to have some idea of where we were because he went downtown to his job but did not know how to get to the art museum. He said he went to the library a lot and that he had some books he wanted to return. He returned them. The library was very nice. There were lots of mosaic tiles in the room before the front desk.

walked to the art gallery we'd been planning to go to. It was mildly difficult to find it, he looked on his phone and we went a bit out of the way but found it after backtracking a tiny bit. He had a backpack and a jacket and a raincoat. I had a light jacket. We waited in line for tickets at the art gallery since it was a free tickets day.
I was somewhat trepidatious entering the museum and wondering how I would feel about art after I'd been apart from it for so long and changed so much and become more complacent in general.

We went to the Korean printmaking exhibit downstairs. We stumbled around somewhat awkwardly in terms of whether to follow each other or to make our own way. I was interested in the exhibit and had a lot of thoughts and opinions regarding the prints however I neglected to talk about them. I was in general rusty from not looking at art for a long time, and felt tired of it almost immediately though I was somewhat interested to look at it all. When we reached the end, we commented that we both felt a bit nonplussed about the exhibit and went upstairs to the rest of the museum. We went to another exhibit. He wanted to see the Italian renaissance part of the museum he said, which is the part I was not interested in. There was also a fashion display in the atrium of the museum. I didn't particularly want to go to that.

At the bottom of the museum there was a connection to the more modern part and in the room where the elevator was there was a clay statue with people sitting at a table, all of them white and shiny and polished and wearing crowns and there was something exciting about the sculpture. I was excited about this art piece and we talked about it and I tried to explain why I liked it. I was excited that I was excited about it and that I liked something and felt something about something in the museum, it was the first thing so far. I stood I think against the wall of the elevator and told myself everything was going to be ok. I don't know why I was stressed out but I felt better looking at that art piece and also somehow renewed my stress thinking of the fact that I had legitimately been stressed before. We went up the stairs that led to the other part of the museum, we studied the renaissance paintings for a small amount of time. I wanted to look by myself when I liked paintings and didn't stand right next to him. We went to the ancient chinese art part of the exhibit and looked at the bowls and plates and things I was very drawn to a suit of armor that seemed to be made for a very small chinese warrior. There was another man standing in front of it and Jon was behind us in a slightly different part of the museum/room. The man started talking to me and commenting on the statue especially about how small the wearer of the suit would be in order to fit into it. The suit had some crazy hair and a very scary looking mask/face to it. I wondered if Jon felt weird that I was talking to someone else as part of our date. I was wondering if I should make it clear that I was with someone else during that interaction or whether I should potentially talk a lot to the guy in order to make it seem that I was not super invested in the date I was currently on. It did seem like somewhat of a relief as my date and I both had nervous energy and the man I was talking to was more confident and I liked saying funny things about the suit of armor. Eventually Jon came to stand right next to me and I stopped talking to the man and continued walking with Jon.
We went downstairs to the part that led to the modern part of the exhibit.

we went to the modern part of the museum. I felt more comfortable here. I enjoyed looking here and felt a sense of connection to the paintings that I had not felt so far, however I felt a loss of some sense of consciousness of what they meant if I had compared it to some things that I had felt connected to in the past. In the last room of the modern exhibit, there were a few paintings that I felt strongly positive about, in fact they were amazing.

As we walked up the stairs to the last part of the museum, I felt there was a sense of camaraderie between us, perhaps connected to us both liking the modern part of the exhibit. We decided to leave the museum after we went upstairs and we discussed feeling somewhat overwhelmed and that it made little sense to put so much art all in one place as it was hard to address and feel something about so many things, especially things that were powerful and required concentration and awareness to fully benefit from and I considered the ideal place for art in the world - perhaps a person's home.

I realized that it had been hard for me to express thoughts that I had to Jon. while in the rest of my life I felt that that was the most common form of interaction and that I was constantly trying to express complex thoughts to people about things that I was experiencing or thinking about, it was somewhat different with Jon seeing as he had been doing a lot of that related to books and philosophy and our respective schools and I felt a loss of my interesting thoughts and somewhat weakened sense of the idea that I had these certain thoughts. It occurred to me for the first time that maybe maybe being alone stop living I was better than being around someone to talk to much because at least then I could have interesting thoughts of my own
After the modern art exhibit, there was a shift from him knowing more about things than me to me knowing more about things than him because I knew more about art and he knew more about books.

there was some tension about who knew more about stuff, whether we liked each other, if we were having a good time, how much we were supposed to be polite, flirt, be interested in each other now that we had established being friends from walking around for this amount of time and talking about things we were both relatively interested in and yet there wasn't an established amount of attraction and we both seemed somewhat nervous. We have a situation we’re trying to figure out the ratio of these things and you probably know this moment I’ll be the right place for you I was surprised to meet someone I felt was similarly smart and interested in things perhaps a lot more interested in academia than I was at the moment.

original: David’s photos were abnormal, emphasizing his creamy complexion. He seemed very young for a man, and was in fact two years younger than me. But after some banter (about cats and dreams), we agreed to meet at an all night coffee house that I rarely visited during the day. When I arrived he had already ordered (a smoothie), and made sure to stand as far from the counter as humanely possible so as not to be confused for the one that was paying; I ordered a chai tea.
I was excited as I pushed the door open to sit under one of the tables with umbrellas - he seemed a bit nerdy, but kinda cute, in a way that excited me.

We sat at a round table and talked about him studying computer science. I forget what we talked about. All I know is that I remember thinking this could be the one for some reason, he seemed cool. I couldn't finish my chai tea and he finished some of it. Then I got a bit annoyed cause he wasn't making conversation. I told him I shouldn't drink the rest of my chai tea or else I would become even more hyper, I felt that I already was talking very fast and asking questions and he was sitting far back in the chair not talking and being quiet.

He said I should drink the rest and see how hyper I could get, which didn't seem to match the impression I was getting so I gave him a few points for that. I gave it to him and he had the rest. We went to my house to get my shoes and then I remembered the thing about having to be someone that the person would like on purpose instead of trying to be someone that the person wouldn't like. I had gone on so many dates that somewhere near the 10 minute mark I felt I had already made too good of an impression, they were ready to marry me, and I knew I would never see them again. Such was not exactly the case, though I can’t say I would have spotted him in a crowd, he was very curious and very stubborn.

When we got to the bus stop, I used one hand to swing freely around the pole and he refused to tell me his height in anything other than centimeters, saying something about the system being flawed. However, he took this very strange hill he’d decided to die on much further than I would have guessed. Needless to say, I still don’t know how tall he is (and perhaps I shouldn’t have asked in the first place). We went to the bus stop. I sat down and hugged the pole of the sign for the bus and said that it was the same as paying the fare and he stayed upright and looked for the bus and checked his phone and told me when it was supposed to come and seemed nervous that it wouldn't come on time. We got on. I didn't have a dollar so he gave me enough to finish paying the fair.
We walked to his house. He had told me about a guy he'd seen with a car full of cats, sitting in his driveway with all the cats for a few hours. He pointed out the house. We got to his house.

He told me his roommate had never once since he’d lived there brought a date over, so this was very surprising to him. He seemed to have some beef with his roommate; something to do with they were both vegetarian but she had recently become vegan and was now shaming him for putting things like butter in the fridge. I couldn’t imagine how two such seemingly polite people might have come to harbor such total and complete resentment. But I supposed I’d seen it happen with best of friends.

We sat at the table, not talking very much and then decided to prepare some pasta for dinner together. He had a giant block of cheddar cheese, which he instructed me to grate which I did so, first using a handheld grate, and then I found another larger grater that worked a bit better. At this point he became very pissy that I’d used two different cheese graters when I should only have used one. Two cheese graters to clean, instead of one. I was starting to see how he might be having difficulty getting along with his roommate.

His roommate came home and she was very peppy. We asked each other basic questions about where we were from etc. and I wondered once again how David had possibly gotten on the wrong foot with her. While we ate our two bowls of pasta at the little wooden table, her date came and they cuddled on the couch and drank beer. They invited us both to sit on the couch with them and watch the movie they were planning to watch which was Lost in Translation.

Next to the couch it seems they had salvaged an old seat from a car, which still had the lever to make it lean back. David sat on the car chair and didn't say anything else after that  and refused the other beer that they offered which I accepted. When they suggested we watch another movie he said that they could but that he didn't want to and that he could take me home if I wanted.

We went outside and went to his garage where he had a motorcycle. It was at that moment that I realized I had to pee. That wouldn’t do for my first time riding a motorcycle. He had forgotten our helmets inside. Panicked, I squatted, hoping I could somehow pee in his shed before he came back but the thought that he would reappear at any moment made me pee shy. He came out and he gave me a helmet and we got on the back and we rode home and it was exhilarating.

He came in and we decided to play a board game and that we were going to play chess and take it outside. We went outside to explore and we tried to go into the sheds that are in the backyard but we couldn't open them. Eventually we decided not to play the game and we stood awkwardly in the kitchen saying goodbye without touching.
LATER ENTRY

He picked me up from my house and we drank beer at the park, then went to his house and played Nooki and fell asleep holding hands with a cat between us. I dreamt that there was another girl in our bed (maybe Molly) who looked like his cat. He went to school in the morning and when he got back we had tea in the kitchen and then we went to Los Gorditos and shared a quesadilla and then we got the ladder so he could go onto his roof and plugged stuff in and cut part of the tree down. original: I met Jake at the Southeast Grind at about ten o’ clock at night. I was watching him through the window as he had a cigarette. I thought he was the most attractive person I’d ever encountered and figured he was passing through and I would never talk to him or anything.

Instead he came to sit three seats away from me at the counter overlooking the window I’d first seen him through. There were three people in between us but after they left, slowly, one by one, he and I were left, and I could see that he was drawing in a sketchbook. I sprawled crazily over all three seats, my stomach resting on the middle one between us but he didn’t seem to notice my strange position when I asked if I could see what he was drawing. He showed me. It wasn’t anything particularly impressive - I think something with watercolors and immediately I was turned off. But I persisted in asking him questions and then he asked if I wanted to play chess.

Of course. He got the board from the games closet and brought it to a two-person table and we set up the board together. He didn’t ask me if I knew how to play, or if I was any good, but instead sat in a sort of interested silence.

The strange dark essence weighing diagonally upon me from his long face held me and became liquid and I fell down, it was the weight of the anticipation that had been born from that moment of staring at him from inside to the outside of the window. I moved my pawn sideways and sagged into leaning on my splayed arms, my head heavy, and at an angle so I could look up at him.

So though we started the game according to the rules of chess as I’d known them from a child, this oppressive interaction, our lack of explicit communication, caused me to act out, and rather than moving my pawn 2 spaces out, I moved it 3. He moved a piece on his side without looking at my side. I moved a knight into a cluster of pieces on his side. He moved his own pieces on his side of the board, I moved pieces into the border on the edge of the playing space, I moved his pieces, I moved two of my pieces at the same time, I slumped into my outstretched elbows with a huge smile on my face and he continued to play the game according to its rules.

I moved pieces that had been dead back onto the game board, I killed my king with my queen and moved it off the board so that no one could win and we continued until he had about ten pieces left and I had only one white pawn that was darting around all of them whether it was my turn or his. “You win.” I said. He agreed and started setting up the pieces to play again. I won the second time. Throughout the games he remained stony face and unperturbed. He followed the rules without comment and then he got up and asked if I wanted to go smoke a cigarette or watch him smoke.
“You wanna…go outside for a…cigarette?” I got up and went with him, retrieving my phone and wallet from the counter area.
I leaned on him, his dark sweatshirt onto mine, in the night, the cigarette in his hand.
“I’m gonna sit down – you wanna – sit on my…lap…?” I felt a little heavy as I positioned my weight evenly across his legs.

Someone he knew approached the café and stopped when they saw him to talk. He was a medium size brown haired boy about 25. They talked for a few moments about some job they’d both participated in, as I stared at him from my perch on Jake’s lap and then he asked how Jake was. He said: “I can’t complain, I got a hot babe on my lap and a hot cigarette on my lips.” I continued to stare silently at the boy. Jake told him that we’d been playing chess, suddenly excited, thinking they could share. “Do you wanna play chess?” asked the boy to me. “No,” I said. He left into the café.

“Is this a…scarf?” he asked, pulling the lining of my dress from my neck. It wasn’t, it was part of my dress. “Yeah.” I don’t like scarves. My face was not facing him. He leaned forward to kiss my mouth but I didn’t turn my head around to face him, instead I turned it the other way so I didn’t feel that we were intimate.
I turned around and put my arms around his neck and my legs around his stomach.
“You’re a little Koala, aren’t you?” he said in something like disbelief.

I told him I lived in Portland and I’d moved a month ago and that I’d just moved from Connecticut. He was surprised, for some reason, perhaps assumed I’d been born in the place he’d met me. I didn’t tell him I’d gone to school there or anything about my life except where I was and where I had been.
He said that he was an artist, and that he came to the Southeast Grind because it was the only place that stayed open all night and he liked to work on his art there.

And then we were walking towards his art studio, he’d invited me to come, it was a long walk, it was in downtown portland, a place I’d seldom explored. He carried the Thomas the Tank Engine backpack I’d taken to wearing, holding it in his hand like a clutch, where it fitted me like a backpack. “Is there anything you want to know about me?” he asked finally, into the silence of our walk. I asked him something unimportant and he answered. He asked me
We passed a garbage disposal building. He said “I used to work there.”
When we arrived, he bustled around making noodles for himself using what I couldn’t imagine were clean pans, nor clean utensils. He had a strange device that was silver and resembled a teapot.
He offered me an aux cord and I put on Gucci Mane, which I think surprised him, because he said: “You like Gucci Mane?” and I said “yes.”

There was a congealed stickiness that followed me in and out of the darkened rooms and I “searched” for the bathroom though I knew where it was. There was a window in the room with the sink that looked out over the dark streets of Downtown Portland and all these plants and a dirty toilet that I rebranded artsy as I had that space in a Brooklyn apartment I’d once lived.
I put on Gucci Mane and he poured noodles into a silver cylinder with a pouring spout. He lit a fire on a gas stove and put the silver cylinder on top of it.
“You like Gucci Mane?” He asked me, and I said “yes.”
I climbed into the corners of his room where there were canvases leaning against the walls in layers of six or seven. I looked at some of them but wasn’t that interested.

I sat down in the chair next to his which was an uncomfortable metal folding one and folded my legs and my arms across my chest. He looked comfortable in the arm chair and he started slurping noodles down. He offered me some, but I shook my head no.
He said he realized he hadn’t eaten all day.
He asked me a question but I didn’t answer him and we lapsed back into silence.
I said “actually can I have some?” Just as he was almost done eating.

As soon as he’d finished his noodles, he said, “Hey, do you wanna go to my loft?” I didn’t answer him. He started climbing the ladder to the loft. My boots made clinking sounds on the metal ladder. It was dark up there and we looked at each other. It just happened that we started kissing and he stopped and replaced a wooden board that was the door to the ladder that went downstairs. He finished replacing the wooden board
“You’re the first girl I’ve brought here” he said with a sort of goofy grin.

In the morning he told me he had to get up in a little bit to go do something and I sat up in bed and started getting my phone and clothes and things. He put his hand around my waist and pulled me backwards so that I was curled up in front of him and said “We can sleep a bit more.” It was warm and soaky in that room now that it was sunny and the morning and I enjoyed him holding me in place. We slept for another hour and then he got up and I got up and I felt this whiff of insanity and extreme airiness. I felt better when I saw when I remembered that he’d been wearing combat boots as I watched him replace them on his feet, pull each lace tight. I imagined they were steel-toed.

He handed me my boots and I didn’t put them on, I paused in replacing my clothing with my boot in hand and then dropped it to the floor as he climbed down the ladder and took a seat in the chair he’d been in the night before. He got a cigarette from his pack and said he was gonna smoke one.
I lay belly down with my head protruding through the hole in the wooden boards to look at him.
“Are you…ok?” he asked me and I said “yes” and I didn’t say anything for a few minutes and said “yeah” as if it was a stupid question.
He asked if I wanted to take a shower and I said “yeah!” He said he had soap and he would find me a towel.
We went into the bathroom
I tried to come into the shower with him, but he explained as though I were a child, that some experiences were personal and that he liked to shower by himself.

Afterwards, he left so I could use the toilet and I was pee shy but instead sat on the toilet staring off into space thinking of that dirty house in Brooklyn with all the plants and the sweet honesty of it that was present here too. Outside the bathroom, Jake and a voice I didn’t recognize began a conversation about girls putting fingers in their butts.

“It happened to me once, in college. I don’t let it happen anymore.” said Jake to his faceless companion. They had a genius idea, together, then - a wooden butt plug that would disallow the possibility of girls sticking their finger in their butts. Eventually Jake came to see what I was doing in the bathroom. He said “You ok in there?” I said “yeah” and came out quickly; giving up.

After that, he walked me to the nearest street corner. ”So, did you want my number?” he asked and I went through the motions of putting him in my phone, using only his first name cause I didn’t know his last, and didn’t care to ask. He seemed to notice my disinterest and told me he rarely gives girls his number. I hugged him around the middle and said “bye.” I walked away and he walked back to his place.

I walked rather purposefully away from the street corner we were standing on and called my friend Adam and then my friend Charlie and then my friend Alessio and walked into a greasy chinese food place and asked if they were still seating and felt timid and different than I usually did, and tired, and the day was new and warm, not that I noticed. I sat down at a four person table by myself and looked at the menu and ordered some noodle thing with beans that was eight dollars and called Adam again and he answered this time and told me he was getting high. I said I wasn’t feeling very good and he asked why and I said I couldn’t tell him and he said “oh” and then he guessed and I said I’d had sex with someone else and that I was upset about it and he told me about being high and about being bored and I felt limp and depressed that he wasn’t interested in my experience and then he got off the phone and I called Charlie again. He was in San Francisco and was eating at a table outside and was dealing with some flies that were attacking his food.

He told me that he was doing well living with Brenda and that he’d been hanging out with George a lot. The food came and it was fried beige hard noodles with salty beans on top I ate a few bites and that was it. I told Charlie I was eating next door at a place called “Charlie’s Sandwiches.” I paid and left the restaurant, still talking to Charlie and he told me about exploring San Francisco and that he thought he liked it and he’d made a friend from berkeley but he wasn’t too keen on making friends with college students and I said it was because he’d sort of escaped something by leaving college early and I said I was living in a buddhist household and he said that that day he’d gotten up at 9:00 which I probably didn’t understand because I got up later and I said, no, I usually got up relatively early and he said that he then walked around at that time which I probably also didn’t understand and what I really didn’t understand was why he was being so mean to me for no reason and even for things that I didn’t need to take responsibility for because they weren’t true or related to my experience at all. I told him this and he just said that in the past I hadn’t adhered to a strict schedule. I told him no my schedule now was pretty normal and that I lived in a house and went out and saw my friends and ate at normal times and that I hadn’t gotten up early that morning because I had spent the night at someone’s house and he’d “forced me” to get up late and he didn’t comment on that and all this time I was randomly walking around downtown Portland, a part I’d never been to. I went into an air-conditioned foyer of something and a person behind the desk shooed me out so I went outside and sat down on the ground in front of the same building and Charlie and I said goodbye and that we should maybe talk again soon. I watched the traffic go by for a few minutes and tried to feel some sense of peace, a sense I’d had more or less stably since I’d lived in Portland as nothing had happened but at that moment it felt like sand was clogging up a lot of my pores. I received a text then from Alessio which said that he felt uncomfortable with our somewhat romantic/sexual friendship and that he could no longer be friends with me or it would feel like he was cheating on his girlfriend. He said that he’d felt uncomfortable with the conversation we’d shared the night before and that he could no longer be friends with me. My stomach dropped and I felt unfair and loud and dark inside, a blue upholstery staining the inside of my stomach and dropping things into my lower abdomen and intestines and stuff and it was silly and bad.

I started walking slowly in the direction of home. I passed a lot of foliage and walked on the side of the highway for a little while and thought about turning to my right and not stopping and then I went behind some bushes and pulled down my tights and squatted and watched people and cars go by and pulled my tights back up and continued walking. I wasn’t upset anymore, I was sad. I felt a little strange. I found a bus stop that I knew would lead me to my home and waited at the bus stop which was across the street from a middle school and watched some boys with skateboards casually talk to each other. I got on the bus when it came, and it was so easy to get home, all I had to do was wait for the bus to get there. I spent a quiet night at home.
“Wanna see my art on my website?” I asked him, and he said “yes, that is something I would like to see.”

My date with Blake was set up to take place in the middle of a forest. He gave me intentionally obscure directions to meet him on a fallen tree at a trail in downtown portland. This, I supposed, was exactly the quirky premise for a date I’d been hoping for, which is, of course, why I agreed. But I was still somewhat skeptical that this seemingly interesting plan would lead to anything as fantastic as it's promise. I didn't let myself set an alarm for waking up in the morning even though I was to meet him at 10 in the morning and I was used to getting up late. I made it out the door with time to spare and I had my roommate plan my route for me using his computer since google maps wasn't working on my phone.

I got on the bus going to downtown but didn't get off at the right stop and ended up going all the way to northeast when I was supposed to get off and switch to the 4. This hiking spot was apparently in the middle of the city

Sun was slanting through the windows of the bus and I while I anticipated this awfully strange encounter, my mind became wrapped up in wondering what all the other passengers might be doing on this strange day where I was neither going to work, nor doing anything else productive. Not only that, but it led me to thinking about people who had lives. And I didn’t have one, I supposed, thinking how I might possibly explain the purpose of my trip. Sitting amongst all these people on their way to wherever reminded me of days when I’d been excused from school due to a doctor’s note, allowed, for once, to lounge on the sunny couches in my parent’s bedroom. I was used to sun hitting them from a different angle, and this slight correction, that it would have been impossible to notice at that young of an age, or even now, shifted my reality a fraction of an inch into an alternate reality where things, vaguely, weren’t as they often were.

There was some confusion with the directions, and as I stared at the spot on the map that was supposedly supposed to take me to my hiking trail, I saw only concrete out the sunny windows of the bus. I thought I must be crazy to imagine that somehow, beyond all these strange streets, I would find myself in an all-consuming wilderness. And so I remained seated on the bus as it took me to the completely wrong end of town.

When I realized my mistake, I began to panic. Waves of caution traversed my body as they hadn’t since I nervously awaited my teacher’s realization that I had not, as instructed, written 6 pages, or constructed a powerpoint presentation. This was a wake up call. Why were there exactly zero moments of this kind of terror in my daily life? I couldn’t remember the last time I felt alive like this, and though it wasn’t exactly pleasant, I resolved to *do more things, *the vaguest of plans.

I texted him that I was late and had gotten a bit lost and he said that he was enjoying what he was doing in his tree and that it would still be there when I got there which was a lot of points for him and somehow I got back to enjoying the sunshine on the exposed parts of my body, the newness of being out and about this early, with or without more than a fleeting sense of purpose.

feeling relatively relaxed despite the fact that there was a potentially amazing boy doing absolutely nothing in the middle of a forest somewhere that I have never been before and I couldn't do anything about that. I was unclear whether to tell him more specifically how off track I was as I waited for the bus going the opposite direction so that I could go back to downtown and then take the second bus that would lead me directly apparently to the wilderness area.

I got off the bus finally and switched. I was recovered from my moment of increasing panic eh oh reminded of when school projects were due when I had ATL been in school that I experienced when I realized how far off I was and how long it would take me to retrace my steps. It was thrilling and I used the moment to reflect on the fact that there was nothing in my current life that caused me to have panicked imminent spoke this and I set a goal of doing more things I had specific things in mind I forget what I think art projects. I arrived at the gas station that was the stop that my route told me was the closest to the park but did not know how to proceed from there.

I walked one direction and then the other and finally got to the trail opening. I proceeded up the trail as instructed, then looked at my OkCupid profile to see the rest of the directions. It said to go past three fallen trees and across two wooden bridges and that I'd then find him. I felt scared and discouraged realizing that I was not sure I was on the right trail and had not come to even one of the trail markers. I went back I texted him. I looked at the message again. I went forward. I stopped and sat down and even though my phone battery was not high I chose to listen to blue by animal collective which had been stuck in my head and to take the moment to feel enlivened and well and to collect myself after the trauma of the night prior. I met two women and asked if they had seen any wooden bridges and they said they had but a little bit farther up so with renewed strength and determination I walked the way I’d been going originally. I became once again confused and felt that I wouldn't find him so I called him and he agreed to me at the entrance to the trail. He approached me where I sat on a bench next to the water fountain which I gulped unceremoniously and appreciated oh god the bountiful water after I had deprived myself in the journey in and drank it with complete delight so much that I felt like a deer at a watering hole which is something I feel like almost all the time anyway.

I made him wait on some tree for 2 hours after I took the bus to northeast instead of southwest. He approached me in a punk rock kind t-shirt and jeans. He was a healthy height and weight and his hair was long. He didn't seem particularly set on impressing me and made very casual conversation about something strange. The moment of us meeting in this strange place was bypassed casually by our lack of acknowledgement and we kept on going. He led me back up the trail to his tree that he'd been inhabiting for the most recent part of his life.

We went to get a burger. On the way he told me all about his weed trimming business and how it was really good for him and how he didn't feel guilty about it and stuff like that. I didn't say anything because I wasn't remotely interested.

I didn't let him pay for me at the burger place even though he seemed to really want to. I knew I didn’t like him, and felt it wouldn’t have been fair to accept free food without reciprocating his affections. We played a game where we each wrote parts of stories on the little pads of paper I brought that were in my purse. I didn't eat most of my burger. I lied about not speaking Spanish so I could prove a point I was making about something and then when we went to the other bar he said that was a lot of points. He asked me on a scale of one to ten how well the date was going for me and I said I didn't want to answer that and he said it was about a seven for him and I asked him his judging system and he said I'd gotten points for persevering on the hike and for pretending I didn't speak Spanish to make a racist point. He told me about his ex girlfriend and how he'd written her senior thesis for her because she was Asian and couldn't write in English that well. We went to sit on the couch where there was a mirror and he had his arm around me and we might have kissed. I said I was really tired and just wanted to take a nap. This was true; I had gotten very little sleep the night before.

Then we had to figure out how to get home and we got on this one bus but it seemed to be taking a super long time so we got off because we thought we'd been going the wrong way but it turned out we hadn't been so we got back on and after we waited in the median. It was nice on the bus because he was self conscious about talking on it because there were so many other people so we just sat with his arm around me without either of us talking much.

When we got home I went in first and laid in my bed and he went to the bathroom and then came to my bed and he seemed to feel uncomfortable and said this wasn't what he'd been expecting and he said he wanted to cuddle and I said I really just wanted to take a nap because I was a little bit disgusted by him because he'd been talking so much. But him trying to convince me made me reconsider because it was an interesting thing to be arguing that we should cuddle and finally he asked me if he was ever going to see me again and I said no and he said alright fine. I stayed in bed I finally got up I said I'd walk him to the bus stop which I found on my gps and waited for the bus with him and waved goodbye when he got on.

That night was strange. I went to the Southeast Grind and saw Jake and he was flirting with this other girl who was blonde and seemed really my and they were both sitting on the couch together and they left together and he ignored me. I texted Adam about it and told him I'd had sex and he gave me advice to tell him I was 14. I never went to bed and instead walked all the way to Hawthorne in the morning. I met this homeless man who said he had been stuck in a parking lot for the past three days because he'd hurt his leg and hadn't been able to get up. I gave him some money and talked to him about how he could get to a doctor since he didn't want me to call an ambulance and and he said he had a friend he could stay with in Salem but he needed enough money for the bus ticket. I suggested he walk into the bus and the fact that he was clearly crippled would make the bus driver let him on for free but he said he'd tried that and that they hadn't. He had trouble even getting to the bus stop which was across the street. I left but then I came back and bought him a burrito from the mini mart and some drink and gave him bus money to get to Salem and he said he didn't want me to come with him anymore.

I walked to a Subway and laid on a bench while my phone charged and Blake texted me when he got off his shift at 9:30 am. I fell asleep on the bench for a little and then watched a family order stuff and leave. I went to the Goodwill but it was a boutique which is not what I was interested in. I went to a bar that also served pizza and ordered some pasta and beer and stayed there most of the day until more customers started coming. Then I went to the back and charged my phone more and watched a large family eat dinner. I left and walked towards home and stopped at Lardo and got a very dark beer and messaged someone on okcupid for a while. I got home and tried to make some plans to hang out with the boy whose number I’d gotten at contact improv but ended up staying home and probably going to sleep.

original: I meet Patrick on the street, and he has just come from the 711 where he has gotten a beer for himself.

Patrick’s carefully constructed hipster outfit incorporates a lumberjack-like plaid flannel, as well as large horn-rimmed frames. Atop his head sits a messy bun from his silky mane of light ginger strands. I am wearing my customary black tight dress with my black skeleton long sleeve shirt on top and my black Harley Davidson boots. I’ve worn it for the past week and a half and none of my other clothes are clean.

On our way, we pass a table where Michael is seated in front of an open laptop. He wears his signature gray cardigan, and what seems to be his only t-shirt whose tiny holes make it possible to make out part of his bare chest, shining translucent in the moonlight.

He gets up and decides to join us to get more beer from 711 and I go inside and buy a very dark porter in a handsome glass bottle. Not a single beer but a 40, much too much for me to drink by myself, but I’m feeling ambitious. Outside, I find them amiably comparing notes on what they hate about America. They are speaking feverishly, gesturing rapidly, and the same word, capitalism, is interjected every few seconds.

Both of them want to move as soon as possible, maybe to China or India where things are cheaper and more community-oriented and there isn’t so much *capitalism. *I can’t quite bring myself to join their \{complaining session\} and I find myself staring blankly at the brazen bumps in the paved lot, and at the white poles holding up the stand, and at the dark night that is behind it all, that I can’t see. The more the merrier, you might think, but no, instead my friend and my date claim each other’s attention so there is none left for yours truly.

An overweight stranger pulls up in a beat up van and as his car fills with gas, he approaches me, and only me, asking if I have a cigarette. I note his gauges, a nose piercing and khaki  shorts, and I am frankly, pleased to finally have a companion of my own.
Patrick says he’ll give him one for 50 cents. The stranger hands him 50 cents from his pocket.

After he takes the cigarette, he goes back to ignoring my two companions. He looks straight at me, and asks, quite aggressively, who these two boys are. I answer frankly that I’m on a date with one and the other is my friend. He asks, looking at Patrick only for the brief moment it takes to gesture at him in reference, whether I feel safe with my date.

“Look, you can’t just like insult my date like that or whatever, ok. He’s like a person and all.” I’m hoping this impromptu confrontation may have the effect that they never utter the word capitalism, at least for the rest of the night.
We pass around all the bottles at least once, through the circle, even though the boundaries in the circle feel like they are constructed from steel string.
Michael says nothing and does nothing, with a shit-eating grin plastered across his face.
“If we were to fight, just saying, you’d be dead. On the ground in one second.”
Michael and I sort of gasp. Chubby stranger looks at him a little more.
Patrick stalks closer and closer to chubby stranger until he is only centimeters from his head, staring at him with his magnificent dark eyes. Like a tiger.
Like a tiger, or like a man trying to prove a point.
Patrick wraps his arm around Chubby Stranger’s back lightly.
“You guys look gay, oh look, I think they’re gay, don’t you think they might be like maybe just a little bit like gay, or something? No? I think they might be.

Michael and I stare at each other across the circle, a hint of mirth on our lips, but confusion in both of our eyes, as our two new friends seem to be squaring up to fight each other. Over nothing. Finally I say, “do you like, really wanna hit something, or what?” to my new friend, now back to acquaintance, “cause, you can just hit me.” He is surprised at first, with a questioning look. “It’ll be fine, I think, no seriously.” We go back and forth, him not believing me at first, until he finally delivers a light slap to the side of my face, but not so light as I was expecting.

After this, I can think of nothing to do but leave, and so Patrick and I make our way quickly back home, while chubby stranger most likely returns to his car, and from the corner of my eye, I can make out that Michael has now seated himself at a nearby picnic table. Tension successfully diffused. To what end, exactly, I can’t be sure.

Now Patrick and I are walking home. He comes in, and I fulfill my promise of letting him sleep in my bed. Except he isn’t ready to go to sleep. All thoughts of that strange depressing day having left my mind, I now simply want to sleep. But Patrick lies awake next to me, pleading that I haven’t gotten a chance to get to know him, that I’ve prejudged him, that I’ve made a mistake.

In the morning, he smokes out of a pipe he brought, and leaves the ashes out on our communal table as marijuana smoke fills the air. I, still in bed, ask him to dispose of this waste but when he finally leaves through the side door, I find it still there, but not before my roommate of this substance free household, sees it.

He texts me later, thanking me for the show. I can only suppose how his account might differ slightly from mine. A strange sentiment and I reflect on the events as I suppose he intends, as though they are the plot of a movie. Still, I think he would be the main character, as I can’t think of anything out of the ordinary that I’ve said or done that night previously, or this morning.

original: Trevor and I met after my lunch with Daisy which was nice. Daisy and I stopped at a coffee shop and Trevor called my phone before the date, asking if I had any ex-boyfriends who might be out to get him. He told me he'd just gotten a call threatening him not to go out with his girl. I told him I wasn't sure who it could be but assumed it wasn't related to me. He seemed unconvinced and a little angry.

He joined me twenty minutes later at the table where Daisy had been. He ordered a coffee with four shots. He was very cute but not very big. He looked a bit like Drake from Drake and Josh. He was wearing skinny jeans and a black t-shirt. I don't remember what we talked about first. He told me he liked to drink tons of coffee. He told me he wanted to see this movie called "Roar" which was edited from footage about a group of people who live with lions to prove that they aren't dangerous. None of the lions were hurt in the making of the film, but apparently almost the entire cast had severe injuries after being in the film.

We got in his car and drove to The Florida Room where we sat on the outdoor front patio. He bought us both tequila shots and he read some of his poetry aloud and then I read some of mine aloud. I went inside and got us mixed drinks and then he bought us a shot of something else and came to my bench and kissed me. He told me he knew the bartender and the bartender always gave him extra-full shots which resulted in me getting very drunk and going to other people's tables and talking to them and then telling them they were boring until he escorted me out.

We walked two blocks to his house. He lived on the top level and I made a bunch of noise in the bathroom. I was pretty drunk and I lay across an armchair he had at the foot of his bed while he sat on his bed. We put on this movie called "Welcome to the Dollhouse" about a girl who gets bullied and likes her brother's friend. After that I found it was my time of the month so we walked about five blocks to get tampons and he got beer.

As we walked up the stairs to his attic room, I noticed some scratches on his face that the light had reflected from above. I asked him about them and he said that his ex-girlfriend had done something to upset him and he'd smashed a beer bottle over his head to try and kill himself. I don’t remember asking him this, but he told me I did the next day. He told me the next day that I fell asleep.

In the morning he gave me the remote and said I could put on any movie I wanted and I put on Hunter S. Thompson's fear and loathing in Las Vegas while he kept sleeping. The morning was sweet and sunny coming in through the window and at first I was ensnared with the movie, especially the colors which seemed so pastel and opaque. I decided it was my favorite movie. As it went on I liked it less. I realized there was sort of no plot.

I stopped watching and rolled over and went back to sleep or maybe we started talking. I noticed that he had an electrical plug on the ceiling and that when he plugged his phone into it, the phone dangled in the air pretty far down and the cord spun. We stayed in bed for a while. Finally we decided to get breakfast. We got ready and I saw that my friend had called so I called him back. I told him about Roar and he told me he had an interview for a job in New York and that the trick was to make it seem like you had tons of offers for other jobs, and we joked about taking calls from other job offers during the interview. I told him I was on a date and that I needed to get off the phone. Trevor seemed a little put out after the phone call.

He drove us to a breakfast place a bit away. He said he had a therapy appointment and therefore would have to drop me off at my house after we had breakfast. He also told me he hasn't necessarily eaten the day before. We each ordered big breakfasts. We were pretty quiet during breakfast and he seemed a little subdued. The waiter was very kean on us and told us over and over that we would like going to Monday Funday. We each paid for our own and since I hadn't eaten much I got a to go container. He drove me home, except there was a ton of traffic going over the bridge and he called his therapist to tell him he was going to be late. He told me his therapist really liked him and wouldn't mind.

When we arrived at my house it was past the time of his appointment and he said it was pretty far across town so he called again and apologized but cancelled. We went into my room and he told me about mount st Helens and how it had erupted and someone had caught it in a picture and sold it to newspapers for a lot of money. I was amazed so we went to the computer and he showed me pictures of it. Then he told me about a TV show where this guy pranked people who had businesses by advising and implementing absolutely ridiculous business promotions. We watched an episode in which he helps a pizza delivery company by implementing a policy which says that if they don't deliver the pizza within seven minutes, the customer gets a free pizza. However, the free pizzas are exactly one inch big so even though they never get pizzas there in that amount of time, it hardly costs anything to give away such small pizzas.

Then we watched another episode in which he makes a haunted house more scary by convincing people that go into it that they got bitten by one of the actors who had a deadly disease. I wanted to watch the one where he is the bachelor and we did. We took a walk around the block and he smoked a cigarette and then I went back and got my shoes and we walked to the Southeast Grind and he got another drink with four shots of espresso. Then we walked to Division and up to Hawthorne and then back to Division.

We started talking to some guy outside a liquor store who wanted to buy liquor but the store was closed. He and my date were from the same part of the state in the south and talked amicably until he met up with his wife and their child who was in a baby stroller. The wife gave us a strange look.

He told me the story about his girlfriend as we continued walking. He said that they'd been homeless together for a while and had gotten very close because of it but now that he had a place to live she treated him badly by never letting him talk to any other girls but breaking up with him often and going out with other boys and then calling him and saying mean things. He said he had been meaning to break up with her but they kept getting back together. He had a destination in mind but it was elusive so we ended up walking back to Division and then stopping at The Whiskey Lounge where he ordered a drink except I hadn't brought my ID so I couldn't get one myself but took a lot of sips of his.

He also ordered barbecue chicken skewers which we shared and I went inside to get napkins to blow my nose with except they were very mean in pointing out where to get them and where to get a cup of ice and it ruined my mood. At the table, we were sitting outside, Trevor told me a long story about something that had happened in his hometown and how he had come to Portland and been homeless in his car for a while and trying to make ends meet except that I wasn't sure why he felt he was the only one who should be talking. I kept asking him questions but also felt like he should encourage me to say something about myself.

We walked the other way on Division after he paid for everything. I became a little resentful that he wasn't interested in anything I had to say. We were near my house but decided to walk across the bridge to downtown because we said we were gonna go to a strip club but he changed his mind and said he was too tired. He played Venus in Furs and another song by the Velvet Underground on our walk across the bridge and it was quiet and both of us knew the words so we sang along to them.

As soon as we got to the other side we turned back. I was curious about the patch of dry land that was beside the river and asked him questions about it. He also was thirsty and I suggested we go find somewhere and then go back but he said there wasn't anywhere for a while so we walked back. He said he was gonna go home but asked if he could possibly get a drink from my house before he left and I said of course and didn't understand why he was trying so hard not to impose since we'd been hanging out now for the whole day and had let me sleep at his house and everything.

He took my hand as soon as we got across the bridge for the first time we'd made contact that day after lying in bed together. At my house I watched something on my computer while he was preparing to leave and he came to join me but then his friend texted him inviting him to a night club.

He described his friend as someone he didn't talk to a lot but often went clubbing with. His friend had a wife and kid at home who he didn't cheat on but he still liked to go out. I said I wanted to come on the adventure and he seemed a little hesitant, saying I probably wanted to get him out of my hair after so long but no, I wanted to come. We went into the bathroom and I took a shower and then he came in but we pretty much kept our hands to ourselves.

We heard my roommate enter and he was worried that he would be mad at him. We left the house and I chose music and we discovered that we both loved the kinks and the talking heads. He got a little lost and the GPS was being confusing and we went across a part of town I'd never been to before that was less commercial shops and things and more long stretches of road and gas stations.

For some reason we couldn't park quite next to the club so we parked on the other side of the bridge and passed through homeless person territory and someone asked him for money. He said this part of town was dangerous and told me some story about a homeless person pretending to be a policeman or something that I doubted was true and looked up on the Internet.

We had to walk across another bridge that night. We made it to the club and met his friend who was wearing a cowboy hat. The floor was white and it had lights underneath it, it looked like that game I used to play with the polar bears called "don't break the ice". There were a couple girls dancing on poles on white podiums but they got down every once in a while and just mingled with the crowd.

I bought myself a mango drink and Trevor bought himself a pabst. I leaned against the counter not talking to either of them and they were in the middle of the dance floor talking to each other. This guy came over to me and started chatting me up. He was Palestinian I think and he kept making comments about how I was too cute to bomb. I declined his offer to buy me a drink. Trevor and I went outside and sat on the curb while he smoked a cigarette. We watched a couple change or have sex in a jeep across the street. And this guy leading a group of other guys passed us, swinging around a crow bar.

When we went back in it was more crowded and everyone was dancing. I went to the front and sort of danced on the little stage. I started talking to this girl who was dancing next to me. This guy started talking to me and he tried to give me a hug but I didn't let him so Trevor gave him a double high five. The guy was wearing yellow neon. Then he dropped his flashlight or something and I found it on the ground for him and he was very grateful. Trevor came up to us and just put himself in between myself and the guy facing me so that now he was having a conversation with me.

We decided to leave and he said he thought the guy was on Molly. We walked a few blocks and then bought pizza from a pizza place that was walk up. The chef came outside and I started talking to him but he lost interest and stared around and then went back inside.
Trevor's friend drove us to our car cause it was all the way across the bridge and we got inside and drove home. We got in bed and I got something to drink.

While I was out of the room, Trevor's ex-girlfriend called and I came back in to find him on the phone with her. She said something about the phone call he'd received right before our date and it became clear that she was behind it. She had used some kind of voice editing software to disguise her voice like a black guys. She started making fun of him and saying his date probably didn't go well and he retorted that he was still on it. She got extremely pissed and told him never to call her again. He was understandably shaken up after his call with her and started talking about how much he hates her and how it would be good for her to never to talk to him again and vowed that he would not call her anymore. He cried a little.

She started calling back and called ten times but he didn't answer and told me how pissed she probably was. At first I tried to make him feel better but I was starting to worry because I had a job interview the next day at eleven and I didn't want to be tired for it. We were lying next to each other in the dark at this point and after a while he acknowledged that he should stop talking about it but he kept bringing it up again and his palpable emotion was causing me to experience secondhand anxiety that I hadn't had to deal with for a while and it scared me. It also made me uncomfortable that he was so obsessed with this other girl despite the fact that we were lying in bed together. I cuddled him at first but then stopped. He was crying.

In the morning he drove me to the place where my job interview was to be held but first we stopped and I bought a coffee and a ham and cheese croissant for myself. He waited in his car for the duration of the interview and texted me to say where he was and that he was napping so that when I came out I found him on a side street. He drove me back to my house and we had a long kiss before I got out of the car. We made rough plans to see each other in the future.
