original: Off to a Rocky Start

We exchanged about six sentences on OkCupid, and then he asked if I wanted to hang out; we made a plan to wear overalls and go to hot topic (for old times sake; to be ironic or whatever). However, on the day of our date, he mentioned that he had been “just kidding” about the overalls, and meeting up at hot topic. He explained that he would rather go to a park or something. I didn’t like that he wasn’t taking our arrangement seriously, no matter how ridiculous the plan had been.Then I told him to meet me at my house, and he said that I could be a murderer, or a rapist, and that he’d rather meet in a public place. Not entirely unreasonable, though I had never experienced this particular qualm. In another situation, I might have been grateful at his ability to ignore gender norms. As it was, due to some recent frustrating experiences with online dating, I reconsidered whether I really wanted to meet him at all. Would I sacrifice the integrity of our (ok, a little silly) arrangement, only to spend the next five hours in the company of someone I could not stand, making meaningless chitchat as they drawled on about their life and refused to acknowledge that their companion might have a life herself?

No thank you I thought to myself, and cancelled our date right then and there. He seemed surprised, so I changed my mind. He said he was biking around the area and that he would call me when he was close so we could meet on the street corner.  I went into my room to look in the mirror and make sure I was wearing appropriate clothes that didn’t scream “I don’t care if you think I’m pretty.” I put on this white ruffly button down that I’d never worn or considered wearing before but I thought it was perfect for my current sentiments.

I put on the roll-on deodorant and since I was going all out I decided to comb my hair with my fingers. I got engrossed in how much I could change the state of my hair and spent the next few minutes pulling my hand in the shape of a comb through my brown hair which seemed darker than usual; and also more malleable.

After that I wasn’t sure what to do since I now had to wait for his call so I let myself fall backwards onto my bed and stayed there half dreaming about absolutely nothing. I got up and went to the phone and he had called seven minutes prior and I called him and he didn’t answer so I went to the meeting spot which was three houses distance and wondered if it made sense to meet him afterall, now that I’d missed his call and wondered if maybe it was better to save myself the torture of talking to someone that I didn’t want to be talking to, and making sure that they thought they liked me. I texted him a few times some pictures of food and animals and smileys blowing heart kisses. I settled down next to a yield sign and studied the percentage of white flowers that had embedded themselves in the grass. I hadn’t been outside yet that day and felt the gentle sun mushing my shoulders forward and my folded knees into the ground sweetly. I wondered when I would get to go back to my house and send more messages to people on okcupid that I might or might not meet.

He finally called me back, saying that he was a few streets from me on his bike. I asked him where he was coming from and he said he’d been at work painting houses His boss, he said, had criticized his work, citing it as the reason for his less than ideal pay. To which he replied “then it’s great that you’re paying me what you are.”

I suggested that this might have been a less than strategic response to which he replied that his boss was often unfair and that he felt it unfair of his boss to make these comments in the first place.

I asked if we could meet for a very short time period so that we wouldn’t have to suffer through an entire date. He was incredulous and pointed out that it would make him feel pressured to be especially witty. I realized that my reluctance to meet him and repeated allusions to boring dates was exactly the opposite of what I wanted to do since the quality that I objected to most on my dates was their lack of confidence, uneasiness and apparent effort to present themselves as worthwhile dating material.

I stopped myself in my own tracks, and left it at an invitation to my little intersection of white flowered grass, where I now felt at home. I told him to not see me as a date but as a friend to be funny with. He told me he was not looking for a long term relationship and agreed to do that. He said he’d been biking in circles and was a few blocks away so he came into view riding his bike like a steed since he was not leaning forward since he had been using his hands to cradle the phone.

I told him I liked his pants and that was the last I saw of him as I have a policy of not looking at anyone I find attractive. His pants were spattered with paint from his job and he said he didn’t like Jackson Pollock and I told him a story about my foreign exchange student liking Jackson Pollock but no other painters which wasn’t that interesting. I asked him if he’d been on any other okcupid excursions. He told me a longish story about a girl that lived in the South who he’d met on okcupid and had dated for a couple of months (over the computer) and who he had finally met in Portland

He described the experience as a horror story. He’d met her and apparently she’d sounded like an asian gangster and used a ton of swears until she started talking about a topic she was passionate about and then she became interesting. She’d brought him to the hotel she was staying at with her friend and they were watching a movie with the friend asleep and she’d started cuddling with him and kissing him and then moved them to the bathroom and initiated sexual activities while her friend lay asleep nearby.
He mentioned something in passing about how he’d seen my profile, and had finally changed his location to Portland to talk to me, which seemed strange, as I thought I’d been the first to message.
We were now walking on some streets that were in between Powell and where we’d met and the streets were not ones I’d been on before. I was barefoot and we went to the park near my house.

“Are you smoking a cigarette?” I asked him and he commented on the fact that I would not have to ask that question if I’d been looking at him which I knew was true and I started laughing and fell down on the grass mirth filled in the wake of imagining having to explain the reasoning behind my policy to him (a policy that had come into effect, for the first time, only that day).

I said “I wanted to know if you were a smoker in general.” He ignored my question and said he was pretty sure I hadn’t actually taken a look at him since the moment we’d first locked eyes which was actually one hundred percent the case and he said that he was disappointed that people always commented on his paint-splattered pants and that they were just his work clothes so he didn’t think they were cool.

I asked him what I would ideally have said something about when we first met and he said the gold chain that was underneath the rim of his t-shirt and I noted quickly that I didn’t have x-ray vision since the necklace was only visible from within his shirt but this elaborate reasoning escaped him and we moved on. I told him I would start looking at him and that I was weird and I tried to look at him. It took me a moment to convince myself everything was the way it always was and when he started talking about something, I shifted my head in his direction for a second. I was very proud of myself.

He brought up his opinions on people who identify as photographers and I agreed with him. I described the family guy episode where Stewy starts taking pictures of beach chairs and hoses in black and white. It felt strange to simply agree with someone spouting my own opinion back to me, and I felt torn between somehow convincing him I felt even more this way than he did, and simply moving on with my life.

He said that his ex-girlfriend had decided to become a stripper because she wanted her life to be more “real,” as though he thought this was silly, and I was of course, compelled to tell him I was an “aspiring alcoholic” for a surprisingly similar reason.

He said everyone in the park was on an okcupid date and we pointed to a couple in front of us that were not wearing much. He said that was the way to do it – that we should be at the park in our bathing suits. I said I didn’t get the awkward online date vibe from anyone. We weren’t the only couple. A pair passed us from behind. Another one was to our side. There were a lot of people at the park, kids on the basketball court, kids on the baseball diamond, adults on the grass, on the playground, on the benches, near the bathrooms and walking on the sidewalk at the bottom of the hill and the end of the park outside of the batter’s cage.
He said he was mostly looking to make friends in Portland since all of his childhood friends had become gangster drug-addicts. I said I had no friends as I’d moved to Portland only recently.

I said did he want to drink beer and we decided to get beers from a store and drink them somewhere outside. We left the park and went across the street to a store that I’d never been but must have sold beer. While he went inside, he told me to watch his bike, and then that I should not walk off with it. I was surprised, and couldn’t think of a reason he would be distrustful of me. I felt, suddenly, profoundly misunderstood. There was nothing I could do. He left it in my hands and walked through the parking lot into the store. He returned with a paper bag and I gave him his bike and we walked away down the sidewalk somewhat aimlessly until we found another park and we sat there first on the ground, and then at a picnic table.

He asked me what I liked to wear and I said I liked to wear costumes sometimes. He said he liked to do that too, that he sometimes dressed as a goth, sometimes wore white tracksuits, or pretended to be gangster. I was surprised and told him that I didn’t know many boys who liked to play dress up.

I told him about what had happened with David and he wanted to know what David looked like and I told him he was this ginger computer programming boy who was quiet and didn’t have any friends. I tried to show him a picture of the boy I’d left with when I was with David but I found that he had unmatched me.

I asked what he wanted to do now and he said he didn’t know and I said I was hungry and I was in need of dinner. He told me he didn’t want to pay for my dinner and I said that was fine. He continued, trying to explain himself by saying he didn’t want to pay for his own dinner. I said we could go to Los Gorditos and he said he knew I’d been about to suggest that. We looked up another restaurant that was a little farther away and started walking towards Los Gorditos since it was unclear whether the other one was closed or not.

I had chugged the last third of my beer in the last few minutes of us sitting at the picnic bench and when I got up I felt unhealthily drunk, like the air had become opaque and and a darker deeper blue. I assigned  myself the task of being extra careful of what came out of my mouth and what I did while I remained in this somewhat altered mindset.

I ordered a chimichanga which was much too large for me to finish and we sat in silence for a bit eating our food. I had to go to the bathroom but refrained. I don’t remember what happened. I know that he seemed to have less to say. I think he told me about his friends or something.

After the meal he said he had eaten too much and felt sick. I felt others might have tried to hide this fact, but he was straightforward, as though he felt it should be my problem too. I asked him what he wanted to do about it. Usually, I felt situations on dates were manufactured, to an extent, to reproduce this kind of support. Yet here it was, in all its real glory, and I found myself hovering uncertainly in its wake. How could one ask for support so casually? I told him he could come over and sit on my couch for a moment to feel better.

At home, I pulled out all the clothes from my closet and introduced him to them one by one. He told me his favorite was a bright orange long sleeve, with a hologram of a dinosaur. He asked me what I’d be doing if he wasn’t there and I told him honestly that I’d probably be on okcupid. He wanted me to show him; to go on it while he was there.

I had been messaging someone about reading poetry to each other and he said I should just write “let’s have sex,” which I did. He responded a few hours later with: “I live in North Portland, I want foreplay first.” Then another message: “Oh I get it.  Oh haha like “we do sex now.’” and then a third message, something about us reading poetry to each other. I supposed the resulting total confusion represented success, at least in his mind.

I showed him my website where I had pictures of my drawings and paintings and he said, strangely: “Oh, I could actually use you for something! I actually really need to learn how to paint and draw. You could teach me.” I agreed nonchalantly, assuming that, as with most things that are exactly what I would want, that this would never actually happen (as it is and has been my dream to give art lessons to a willing pupil). So I feigned disinterest, and then thought better of it and said “No, I’m seriously interested in that, I’ve always wanted someone who was like actually serious about learning how to draw that I could put energy into and work with for a longer period of time.”

We were in front of the computer and I found the paper cards that my roommate had shown to me that morning and I gave them to him so we could play. He started pulling them out of the pack one by one and reading them to me. I said whatever experience I could think of that was related to the card. We ended on a weird joke about batman being pronounced batmun, that I didn’t actually think was funny. He seemed to be having a good time though.

He told me about this girl Miriam that he was friends with and was having sex with too. He said that she was tough on the outside, but that he felt that she was actually pretty sensitive on the inside and he said that she was having a hard time dealing with the fact that he didn’t want to date her and wanted to have sex with her. He said that once in a while they’d be lying in bed and he’d be tired and would just go to sleep and she would get really weird and he would ask her what was wrong and she would say “Everything, Gabriel, everything.” which meant that she couldn’t deal with him not wanting to be her boyfriend even though they were having sex.
He seemed to be saying also that he wasn’t interested in a relationship at that time.

He said “I have no idea why I’m just like spewing all this stuff at you all of a sudden” and I instinctively responded by trying to make him feel less self-conscious. It made sense, I said, that he was just like telling me stuff, or that like, I was like interested like and there wasn’t anything particularly that interesting about it but I was just still like interested in him and what his life was like.
In truth, it hadn’t seemed strange until he’d mentioned it but now I wondered - why was he spilling these things to me? Did I make him feel comfortable, with my wide, non judgemental eyes?

He told me about the group of friends he had been friends with when he’d lived in Portland earlier and how they’d all become gangsters who spent their lives taking xanax and drinking and that he hated it and didn’t want to be part of it anymore and wanted to get away with it and was hoping to meet new friends on okcupid.

He told me a story about “being assaulted” in which a girl came looking around for something followed by a short man who came looking for the same thing. His girlfriend threw a beer bottle at him as he was walking away and he came back and hit not his girlfriend but him with the six-pack of beer that was next to them. While he was telling this story, I was sitting on the black and silver chair that is right next to the bathroom in the kitchen and he was leaning against the sink, acting it out somewhat.

We went outside for  him to have a cigarette and I changed my answer to a question he’d asked me before and he noted that I was likely psychotic. I agreed and admitted that I sometimes lied about silly things like what I’d had for breakfast while remaining vigilant about recounting things that were best left to the imagination such as my consumption of hard drugs to my mom. We went back inside. He sat down on the couch and I pulled up the black rolling chair so that it was facing him and he told me the long story behind losing his virginity apparently against his will. He’d been 15 at the time and had just run away from home and a girl who went to college had brought him home to her dorm room and he’d been too drunk and high to consider the situation or consent. I told him the story about losing my own virginity.

He told me that it was late and that if he was planning to bike back to his house he had better get going right then. I asked him how far the ride was and if he felt safe biking at night and things like that without saying anything about the possibility of him staying over but without saying particularly that he should leave either.

We went outside together and he got his bike and he was standing behind it on the path that leads to the steps that lead to the front door. It was dark and I couldn’t see all of him, just a glowy outline of a person, a white one with not much height but nevertheless some sort of presence. He looked so forlorn where he was standing behind his bike and I was still standing on the porch, under the light I suppose, and I hadn’t gone down with him when he went to get it and it left him without the opportunity to either hug or kiss me goodnight which is what I perhaps intended. I asked him once again if he felt safe biking so late and he said he did and I said “Alright, see you later.” And he said “Alright see you later.” and I said that if he really didn’t want to bike right then, that he could sleep on the couch and he said he would feel degraded to sleep on the couch.

I said “Oh, do you still want to do like art lessons soon?” and he said “Oh yeah, can I just like start coming by if I’m in the neighborhood?” And I asked if he was being sarcastic cause that seemed like a strange thing to ask at the end of a first date. He said he just wanted to know and I said “Um, yeah, sure, I guess you can come by…” It felt strange to be on the receiving end of hearing something quite so crazy. In truth, I wouldn’t have minded, but didn’t want to say yes in case it were a test about how I would react. And he went to the front door and went to the bathroom first I think and I gave him some water.

He called me about twenty five minutes after he left and said he’d forgotten his backpack at my house and could he come back and get it. I said he could of course and he came back and got it and this time I gave him a hug goodnight.

I slept on the couch that night, with the light on at first, and with my blanket being the sweatshirt that I’d been wearing, the one that Devin had given me but not for keeps but I’d taken it home. I left on videos of Russell Brand and then a variety of other British actors and famous people being interviewed on an English talk show. I woke up at around four in the morning and my sleep had been weird, and I turned off the talk show that kept switching to new episodes on youtube. I went back to sleep still on the couch and woke up refreshed in the morning when my roommate Greg came home from wherever he was. I was still tired and managed to go back to sleep even though it felt like maybe I’d already woken up for good.

original: Date with Michael Kirschbaum

I met Michael Kirschbaum at the southeast grind on numerous occasions, none of which turned into hanging out outside of the bar or in us exchanging phone numbers or making plans to see each other again. Unbeknownst to me, I was also messaging him on okcupid however I did not connect the situations, since his profile picture was blurry. When I first met him I recall becoming increasingly frustrated that, though I was trying to have a conversation with him, he continued to use most of his eye contact on his phone screen, scrolling up and down and clicking on various buttons looking up at me every now and then while still amazingly also managing to dominate the conversation, which was about colleges and which major it is best to partake in, in order to make a lot of money. I continued this conversation only because it was so ridiculous and I was waiting for my chance to point out how rude he was being. However, eventually he became interested in it enough to stop looking at his phone for extended periods of time and I grew out of trying to want him to realize the ridiculousness of his actions because the conversation was actually sort of interesting. We had both lived in Brooklyn for a while and tried to figure out if we knew the same places.

When we met other times, we did not greet each other enthusiastically as friends, but rather as Patrons of the same restaurant establishment who were interested in conversing to keep each other company and to pass time, he did sit next to me though if we entered the cafe at the same time. On one occasion he was already sitting with a boy called Matt who turned out to be extremely political and an activist and talked to me about his activist tendencies for a while. At first I liked him a lot since he seemed to be so passionate about his ideas, but soon grew to think he was unreasonably idealistic. Eventually I stopped talking to him and started talking to Michael who was sitting on his other side and I think we talked about physics or science or something. This time we decided to visit a nearby pancake house which was also open all night and at the last moment, I invited Matt with us too so it wasn't really a date. When we got there we met a homeless guy called Jason, and I invited him to our table as well without realizing how batshit he was. At one point he asked me to marry him and took off the glass pink ring he was wearing and gave it to me which caused his finger to bleed and so I asked for a bandaid for him because I felt guilty and thought maybe I wasn't supposed to be talking to him and shouldn't have invited him to sit with us. Michael and I were the only ones left and we started making lots of jokes about Jason and then we went back to the cafe where we I presume continued to hang out until my therapist came and whisked me away.

Anyway, I had not seen him in a long time since neither of us frequented the cafe anymore and I hadn't even been in Portland except for once when I saw him sitting at one of the tables by the window at the Powell’s bookstore cafe and talked to him for a minute about how he was dating Elise, who had worked the southeast grind except that he seemed unsure of the situation since he said he saw her twice a week and he suspected she might have other boyfriends besides him. After that I left.

I kept wanting to go home since I knew I had planned a date with David Westgate for the next day in the morning loosely in which I was supposed to be giving him an art lesson. His tactic, it seemed, was agree and then ignore, as he would say things like “oh yeah, it’s getting very late, we should probably go home,” laugh, and then start a new topic of conversation. Eventually I simply leaned back against the wall in my booth and fell asleep there for a moment. This time while we were hanging out, we discussed making an app called "niplr" which would be a dating sight where people would meet and decide to meet based solely on pictures of each other's nipples. He also said he wanted to make an app where you could pay for your food in line and I thought that was much too practical and not interesting, and wasn’t sure he understood the game we were playing anymore. I vaguely invited him to my house, saying he could work on his computer while I slept, and he seemed to consider the possibility but eventually went back to the cafe again. The thin morning light was already emerging over the trees and it looked as though it were going to be a gray day. I had less thoughts than usual, due to my sleep deprivation, which was a bit like being on drugs. And though I had been aching for my bed, I didn't go directly home. First I visited (walked by) the bar that was right down the street, and then I boated Alpha who was sleeping in the tree house next door and potentially woke him up except I hadn't seen him in a while and of course he got very excited about something and we highly of an idea to do but never did it.

We matched on okcupid and began an inane conversation of nonsense for a while and then one day he invited me to come to a maker space that happened to be two blocks from where I currently was. I went there and visited him while he was in conversation with someone else: an Asian girl who was sort of aggressive and awkward at the same time. They were talking about college or which colleges they had gone to or decided to go to. I joined their conversation simply by standing next to them but neither of them acknowledged me for a little while until Michael waved his hand in my direction, saying I'd also gone to college in Boston. referenced me, saying I had also gone to college in Boston, except I hadn't, I'd gone to college on Connecticut, I was mildly impressed that he had remembered anything about me since when we talked in the cafe he didn't necessarily give the appearance of actually listening and I didn't necessarily remember anything particular that he had told me either; it seemed a long time ago that we had spoken.

Finally, after a lot of dallying around the beer and the name tag table and going outside to take a phone call from Molly, who I’d hung out with the night before, I began talking to the girl by myself and Michael went to go make himself a name tag too which read "lobster bisque" upon his return. I wasn’t sure this was funny, but told myself perhaps I just did not understand the joke. I came back with my tag that said Sophie and told her that wasn't even my real name because she told me her name and told me what it meant and said that I had a normal name and I wanted to say that I didn't so I told her my name had originally been Sage and she told me I was a coward for changing it to be more normal. I didn't agree that that was the same reason I'd described to her but liked that reason better so I pretended to identify with it. I left this  conversation to get beer and eventually, after I had two panic attacks about what kind of beer to drink and even poured some of one out and left it behind the station and tried the other one and was still anxiously undecided about which beer to pursue or what to do about the alcohol situation in general, Michael wandered over hesitantly and I bridged the gap between us. Then we had a conversation that began with myself admitting to having slept with a girl the night before and told him that her boyfriend had then tried to sleep with me separately and explained how silly I thought this was considering her girlfriend was being cool enough to let us sleep together in the first place and what was the reason that he needed to go behind her back and sleep with me separately, secretly while she was sleeping as well. He even covered my mouth so I couldn't make any noise. I didn't tell him that. He said when I apologized that no the story was very good and that we should probably tell all the people at the party. And we looked around but didn’t want to tell any of them. Then we talked about Sigh, (our mutual friend) and we discussed GitHub and my brother and our app niplr which he made a file for on his computer and we decided to write a comic book, meanwhile the Asian girl he'd been talking to was wandering around the party by herself, occasionally stopping close to where we were and staring at us, I felt worried that we had abandoned her, or that I had stolen him from her; I kept mentioning that maybe we should include her and then going back on it because I didn't actually really want to. Two boys came up to us at different times while I was there and I sort of flirted with them, one of them had his ping pong ball roll over to me and I picked it up but refused to give it to him and he had to come over to me and retrieve it. Another one I may have given him a new name tag. After I took a shot from the cap of the vodka bottle against his recommendation, someone came around and said the party was wrapping up. He tried to decide and eventually took his beer cup with him, covertly next to his waist, outside. After I gathered my books and my packet of memes and weird embarrassing references to the various relationships I'd had in the past month. We walked out into the night, not entirely sure what to do to proceed and I sort of invited him to my house which was far away and he said we should just go to his apartment because it was close, within walking distance, and we met one of the boys I’d been talking to when we went outside and I suggested he give us both a ride on his motorcycle and we all discussed that for a little while and then Michael realized he had to retrieve his charger from the room of the party before the door closed permanently, locking it in so we went back. We eventually abandoned the guy on the motorcycle, and on our walk back to his apartment which was a slight bit longer than I anticipated, perhaps because at this point I was quite drunk, I hurled my meme packet into the bushes at New Seasons and also went inside and took a small sample of macaroni and cheese with my hands and went out the back entrance because I had barely eaten anything that day, if I did eat at some point I don't remember what it was. Which was probably why I was so drunk so immediately. I also hurled my picture books into the bushes in front of New Seasons, and actually I hurled the meme packet into the dog cage where I had once been, myself.

When we got home I was so drunk I simply laid on the sofa and then actually we went onto the porch and a woman was passing by who seemed to be moving out of her apartment and I asked her for food and she went inside and gave me two packets of ramen and Michael and her were having a conversation while I took them and I don't know what it was about since I wasn't paying attention.

dates.dek: Thick pancakes in the morning, then he asked me to leave.

spans.t: He let me sleep in his bed with him but I refused to let him kiss me He made me thick pancakes in the morning He asked me to leave so he could get ready for work He was playing a rap song called “animal” that I liked We tried riding home on his bike with me on his back He offered to pay for a taxi for me He said he was a very good car salesman and worked so much that he needed to use OkCupid He switched my drink order to non-alcoholic He paid for everything, including the drinks I’d had before he came He shared a room with a girl he was not dating As dictated by our weekly Vision Action Group Meetings, I had an all day meeting with my friend Joey.

When the meeting seemed to be dragging I asked if it would make sense if I left him with some alone time. He didn’t mind my being there, he said, before locking himself in the bathroom for half an hour and coming out to tell me some alone time was what was called for. I left with the unnecessary awkwardness of the situation lingering in the pit of my stomach.

Instead of going home I had a drink at a sushi restaurant on Alberta. After I’d been sitting at the bar by myself for about a half an hour I thought of a potential solution. I fired up the ol’ dating app and started inviting people to meet me. I invited three people and two responded and one came and his name I don’t remember.

I’d been sitting in the same swivel stool for an hour and a half by myself, wondering why my life was so boring and what the difference between being alive and dead really was in this moment when suddenly this lanky blonde man came in, nonchalantly taking a seat next to me. He ordered a drink and struck up a conversation as though we had no meeting planned.

After I’d been sitting at the bar myself I started asking people to meet me. I asked three people and two of them responded and one came and his name I don’t remember (it was jake, I think) but his username was pratfaller. I’d been sitting there for an hour and a half by myself and suddenly this lanky tall blonde-haired guy came in, acting nonchalant as though he didn’t know me and took a seat next to me at the bar and started talking to the bartender and ordering a drink.

I suppose his plan was to tell people we just started chatting at this bar, and never mention the existence of our online communication. But we got chatting and he told me he was a very good car salesman and that the only reason he was on okcupid is because he worked so often that he didn’t have time to meet people.

Strange I had never felt the need to excuse my online dating profile (my life’s blood, the precious gem of my existence). He worked sixty hours a week. He’d lived in Portland all his life he liked biking he made a lot of money he didn’t like his job that much but he was good at it.

I was a little gone; I’d already had two drinks and he bought me a third and himself a third too. I got up to go to the bathroom and remember the revelation of walking down the hall without the pressure of my meeting people costume and trying to have a realization about something about life and nothing was coming to me.

When we got up to leave, he paid for not just the drinks he’d ordered with me but the drinks I’d had before he came with his plastic money machine and signed a white little paper. He took me to a bar down the street and we sat at the counter on two black bar stools.

He seemed to know the waitress there and talked to her for a minute while I went on my phone or something and then he ordered a different drink than I asked him to order: one without alcohol. It took me a little longer than it should have to figure out what he’d done and then I was disappointed because I wanted to get a little more intoxicated I was slipping off my bar stool and messing around with my purse backpack and left to go sit at the fire pit.

I sat there and thought about being unhappy. He came to sit next to me and I was feeling warm and sleepy and not like pretending anything anymore. I have no idea what we talked about; if anything I think he revealed that my new drink didn’t have alcohol. He said his apartment was a 20 minute walk and that I could come if I wanted to.

So I suppose I said yes because next thing I knew we were out in the cold night again, traveling for what seemed like forever to a place I’d never been before that I could not imagine actually existing I wasn’t wearing pants; instead I was wearing a skirt. I kept asking him how much longer the walk was going to be and he kept saying like 20 minutes.

He had his bike and he said he’d have a cab called for me if I wanted and that we could see each other again but I was stubborn and we continued the journey. He offered to have me ride on his back as he biked. It was extremely hard to get on and I wobbled off almost as soon a we started moving.

He said we should try again but it wasn’t a good experience and he wasn’t being nice to me so I said no we could just walk the rest of the way. It took a lot longer. I was drunk and said whatever came into my head. I wasn’t walking very straight either; I remember my limbs were falling all over each other sort of and I felt sort of like a frat bro.

I felt like a very clumsy girl. I couldn’t tell if he liked me at all. I didn’t like him too much then either, since he kept saying slightly mean things to me about my being drunk my not having a job. His building was unexpectedly tall, sleek, and shiny. There was even a lobby with brown carpet and marbled tiles.

And to my surprise, we weren’t even the only one’s arriving here this late; in fact about 5 other people took the elevator alongside us. I was excited to be inside. I didn’t look at him and he didn’t look at me. It was a really silent and calm experience after that strange walk and I felt nothing like I’d felt outside in this warm refuge.

When we got into his little apartment I was surprised to find that he had a female roommate, who’d apparently agreed to sleep on the couch due to my presence. She was small, and maybe Asian, and had all her bed things settled there; a brown duvet, and a fluffy white pillow. I talked to her for a bit before dropping all my things onto the floor in his bedroom where we slept on his twin, perhaps cuddling but I refused to let him kiss me.

I don’t know why. I simply didn’t want it to happen. In the morning he was already awake, tossing some pancakes which we ate at his high table. I remember he had a little speaker over which he played an upbeat rap song which I liked, and I asked him for the artist. I do not know what the mood was that morning; I was very grateful to him for making me pancakes, especially after not letting him kiss me.
I don’t think either of us knew if we’d ever see each other again as we boarded the elevator so that he could be on his way to work.

dates.name: Sean
dates.dek: The least successful Tinder date of all.

spans.t: This was perhaps the least successful tinder date of all and actually ended in something like a fight. After spending the night at Jake’s house, I was relatively stranded in a part of town that I did not recognize. I figured this was as a good a time as any to get to know new parts of the city, and found myself in a sports bar with a balcony overlooking giant tvs.

Instead of a bar, they had picnic tables dispersed scattered throughout and I spent most of the day here. I talked to a friend on the phone as I wandered upstairs though that part was roped off and thought dejectedly about my constant, nagging loneliness. How could it be this hard to find people to shoot the shit with, besides my friend’s back home?

I left and made plans to meet Sean Niesson on the corner of Everett and 18th….it was kind of a strange place to wait, and I felt rather self-conscious as cars whizzed past me, probably wondering what I was doing standing in the middle of nowhere. It was then, of course, after I’d finally secured plans, that my roommate Alpha asked if I wanted to meet him at The Economics of Happiness Conference which was downtown.

I said I would meet him and go out for dinner with him and a group of friends he’d met at the conference. Sean picked me up on the street corner of Everett and 19th. I remember because I waited in that corner for quite a while, unsure if I’d be waiting there forever. I got into the car and he was immediately unfriendly.

I don’t remember what we talked about. When I got in the car, he did not smile, and barely looked up. Rather than friendly banter, his hands were glued to the steering wheel, his eyes fixed on the road. I have to say I pride myself on being somewhat of an expert at drawing even the stubbornest introvert into casual conversation, but this time it was really like pulling teeth.

The only thing I remember from this conversation is him being surprised that I had a friend, one friend, who lived in Portland, having lived there for three months. He told me he still hung out with his friend from high school, which didn’t sound too bad to be honest. The conference took place in a large hall, that felt a bit like a church I’d been to once.

The seating was stadium style, and the seats were beige, and cushioned. I can understand, in retrospect, that I might not have been the ideal date, at least from his perspective. While he paid rapt attention to the goings on below, I surreptitiously looked at my phone, which had me quite addicted at this point in my life.

It was the last day of a three day conference, and there was a ceremony wherein everyone was invited to get up and dance. At this point, we switched roles to some extent as he faded shyly into the background, and I joined the lively procession from the hall to the lobby. Outside, we settled on a nearby bar, the cheerful tortoise which I’d never been to before, and as we walked the five blocks over the cobbled stones of downtown Portland, I was somewhat surprised to hear that he’d taken in the message, not to mention on board with its way of seeing the world.

Though I hadn’t, perhaps, been paying full attention, I’d managed to take in enough to know I had my doubts, and tried, a bit unsuccessfully, to explain my skepticism. Oh, what was I doing anyway, casting aspersions on what seemed to be an inspiring experience for the young lad? At the bar, I asked for a dinner menu.

This is when our date, which hadn’t been going particularly well up until this point, sort of imploded. It would seem that he was under the impression that I was trying to get him to buy me dinner. Having had nothing but those thick pancakes early that morning, and having finally arrived at an establishment meant for eating, my mind was occupied with nothing but my sudden realization of hunger.

He paid for our beers, and we left, but as we walked back into the street, we sort of stopped interacting, and he left without so much as a “bye.” I was now out on the streets of Portland by myself and it was getting dark. What’s more, my phone wasn’t charged. However, I managed to find an outlet hidden at the base of a telephone pole and just in the nick of time too, as I’d forgotten I’d apparently scheduled another date that was supposed to starting imminently.
In fact, unbeknownst to me, a man had driven from nearby Beaverton, and was sitting, now, in his car, waiting to meet me.

dates.name: Matt
dates.dek: One tiny blurry picture of him playing a red guitar.

spans.t: Matt’s had only one picture on his profile and it was tiny and blurry and depicted him playing a red guitar. However, our conversation on okcupid had entered the realm of absurdity and I was excited to meet someone who’d been conversing with me exclusively about chickens for a day or two. He appeared above my perch by the telephone pole, where I was huddled, still trying to charge my phone.

He wasn’t quite as skinny as those few pixels had made him seem, and he was wearing a gray sweatshirt. He told me his plan was to go to Ground Kontrol, a bar that doubles as an arcade. But at this point, I was all but starving so I redirected us to the nearest restaurant which was a sophisticated Italian place with counter service and only about 5 dishes on the menu.

We split a plate of pasta and a beer and, after my previous date, we split the tab as well. Afterwards we did go to Ground Kontrol. When I asked him if he’d had much luck on okcupid, he told me a story about the other girl he’d met on okcupid who he didn’t like.

Apparently she texted him that she had been waiting in her car for a while and had gotten very sweaty. I started talking to this guy at the booth next to us who was from Colorado. Then my date and I left. He offered to drive me home. I was a little bit drunk and I discovered I’d forgotten to close my tab so he drove me back to Ground Kontrol and I recovered my debit card.

In the car outside my house he gave me a tiny kiss on the lips before I got out. I went inside and saw that he had texted me that he was sorry if he’d “forced the kiss on me.” I didn’t respond I felt awkward as he hadn’t particularly forced me to kiss him, though I can’t say I wanted it to happen either.

Unsure of how to respond, I didn’t. And later, I found out he’d deleted his okcupid after that, apparently so embarrassed about this ambiguous interaction that he’d wanted his online presence to disappear. A few months later, I sent him the invitation for writing a synopsis of how our date went. He didn’t write one but called me one night while I was having dinner with my roommates.

I took the call in the bathroom. He told me that he hadn’t been on any other okcupid dates after ours and that he thought okcupid was home to the kind of girls he didn’t like. It seemed like he meant basic bitches. He said that he’d been confused because he’d thought our date had gone really well but after it was over he reconsidered why he thought that and couldn’t come up with any reasons.

He said that I’d seemed very nervous throughout the date and thought I must have been nervous to be on a date with him but considered that I might somehow be fucking with him and just pretending to be nervous. He said he didn’t know why he’d had us go to Ground Kontrol and that it was because he had planned it and so it was set in his mind.

I was enjoying our conversation and laughing a lot. He told me a story about his roommate peeing on his living room rug that I found hard to believe. I told him I might hang out with him as friends in a few weeks after I became not so busy.

dates.name: Kyle
dates.dek: In one picture, a chin like a witch.

spans.t: In most of his pictures he looked normal — skinny, with pale skin, my type. In one picture, it appeared he had a pointed chin, like a witch. I wondered — was this the most accurate representation of what he actually looked like in real life? I messaged him for a while, I asked him first for a drum lesson and he countered with: coffee or tea? he asked if I thought that was too forward and he interpreted my “yes” as “yes that was too forward.”

I exchanged a phone number with him, but still had surprising difficulty agreeing on a where and when to meet, even after conversing verbally multiple times. Finally, I led him to my favorite spot, due mostly to convenience (the Southeast Grind) for a coffee or tea or something, though it was already really late at night.

I got there before him, I ordered a chai tea that I did not want but felt obligated to consume anyways, I got a call from him, he arrived on his bicycle; I did not see him when I went outside to look and became concerned that I’d given him directions to the wrong place.

Then I saw him, he had the thing I’d thought his face might look like in his profile, sort of like a witches, with a pointy chin and I thought he was also attractive, more so than my last date at least. He was wearing a sleek black “biking’ jacket and I think shorts, which I suppose did not become him (his personality).

We hugged. He didn’t order anything in the cafe, he wanted to go to subway, there was some awkward confusion with me trying to make up a reason why I would also want to go to Subway but it turned out he didn’t care one way or the other. He seemed not incredibly mindful of what I might be thinking at any given moment.

We went to subway. In the line, we talked about our parents, and their jobs. After we walked the few blocks to his drum studio (about 10), and we made forced and very awkward conversation in the small carpeted space that he was renting. I was beginning to feel rather nonplussed by this experience when he showed me what he could do with drumsticks.

In spite of myself, I was impressed, though less so that he seemed to know and think it was impressive himself, too. We sat across from each other at the makeshift table in amidst various stands and paraphernalia, awkwardly perusing each other’s music libraries, noting intermittently when we recognized or liked a song in common.

It wasn’t going very well; and for a moment I felt I’d been transported back to middle school — unable to carry on a full conversation with the opposite gender, reduced to blushes and quick glances of eye contact. I don’t think I knew what he was thinking. I felt for sure he could have ended the date at any time had he not been into me so I assumed shyness.

We plodded on, and finally we had had enough and agreed it was time to go. But first I asked to use the bathroom and he showed me the way. He noted offhandedly that it was cold and I offered him my coat. Veering from his script, he suggested that we switch outfits altogether, and so we did.

He tried on the black evening gown I’d purchased for \$6.99 from Goodwill earlier that day, and I put on whatever he was wearing. There was something incredibly comical about the large protrusion that appeared suddenly in the front, lower half of the dress, bunching the silken material, rippling outward. Back in the little room he was renting, I picked up one of the wooden sticks that littered the floor and used it to find the indentation of his belly button, then penetrated it rhythmically.

After we spent a bit more time in the studio, he walked me home and slept in my bed. In the morning he told me really liked me, and went off to school. alternate: Memoir — 3 days ago — with Kyle Kyle went with me to the subway where he got a foot long with all the veggies but olives and extra jalapenos.

I got a 6 inch with pepper jack and vegetables and olives and mustard on it whereas he brought chipotle sauce and we sat at a table and he had his whereas I put mine away in my backpack. In the line he told me he knew computer programming because he liked web design. I told him I had moved to Portland from Connecticut and California before whereas he had moved to Portland to go to PSU and his parents kept changing where they liked for his father’s job which was for pharmaceuticals — he didn’t know what disease his dad was caring but I said it was probably Parkinson’s which was a disease I learned about in neuroscience.

dates.dek: Four a.m. was mid-day to me.

spans.t: Due to my strange sleep schedule, 4am had become a normal time for me to be awake — about the equivalent of mid day — and I didn’t think twice about inviting someone over in the middle of the night. However, when he came over toting a six pack of cider, the implication hit me hard and I scooted slightly away from him, not liking his goofy demeanor.

I sat down cross legged on the porch, thinking it would be warmer in my bedroom but not exactly anxious to invite him inside, considering the uncomfortable situation I found myself in. What’s more my bedroom wasn’t big enough for much more than a bed so that’s where we’d have to hang out. I was wearing a skirt that pulled up a little when I sat down but I remembered it was too dark to catch much of a glimpse.

He sat a little too close to me and I moved back a little and the decision not to hook up with him was made explicit, at least in my mind. He opened our ciders. I drank my first five sips in like one minute. We went back into my room and I set up my little plastic horses and cows on a book and then took the bowling pin from my little toy bowling set and used it to knock them down.

We got into bed and he tried to cuddle with me but I was already facing the other way and didn’t let him touch me and at one point he tried to kiss me. I was feeling tired as I fell asleep I think. In the morning he was there and he told me that he’d gotten a boner in the night and hadn’t known what to do since I’d been asleep.

I wanted to say “fat lot me being awake would’ve done” but instead left his foolish thought to hang in the air. I pulled out two eggs from the refrigerator and turned up the heat on the skillet. I cracked the eggs and they all broke. I left them on too long and they got burned on the bottom and then I didn’t flip them over.

I put bread in the toaster and put the egg on it. The eggs had little pieces of black burnt charcoal on them. I asked my roommate whose lettuce was in the fridge and he said that I could use it so I sprinkled some on the burnt eggs. He said they were the worst eggs he’d ever seen.

I decided never to make breakfast for anyone that came over because it never worked and I didn’t even want to. We each ate a few bites and went back into the other room. He laid in my bed for a while. He told me about a date he’d been on the day before in which he’d driven his friend Sarah somewhere and that they’d had a date in the car.

I told him he shouldn’t be giving people rides for no reason and he said he always did it and it was no big deal. He said that he’d been on the hockey in high school and that he and his co captain had had a thing and that he’d never really gotten over her.

He said they’d been pretty good friends before their feelings were talked about but that they weren’t good friends anymore and that he thought about her all the time and wished that he could be with her. He offered to give me a ride to my friend Amicia’s house and I accepted and then Amicia canceled.
He asked me if I would ever hook up with him and I told him never.

dates.name: Robin, Blake, David & Sarah
dates.dek: Everyone at once, starting at a burrito place.

spans.t: It was about three o’clock in the afternoon and I had yet to leave my house, nor did I have any particular plans to. Not only that but I was getting mighty hungry. So when my date from the previous week called me and then texted me that he was at a burrito place and wanted to bring over a burrito and his apparently new girlfriend Sarah, it seemed a little silly to say no, even though I hadn’t had a very good time on the date with him the first time and hadn’t really planned to go on any more with him.

But his girlfriend was coming, so I figured there was no way he could try to hook up with me. Besides, didn’t I always say I wanted to make some girlfriends in Portland? We went to the park with our burritos because we also wanted to drink the lovely dark six-pack they’d brought and my house was one of sobriety, as I may have mentioned previously.

We went to Brooklyn Park which, despite being two blocks from my house, I had never visited. We sat at a picnic table near the edge of the park — underneath the sky which was slowly fading to night. Sarah and I found that we had a few things in common: we were both from LA, we both liked photography, and our parents had encouraged us to follow similar paths in our lives.

Then Robin apparently felt he wasn’t getting enough attention so we changed the topic to one that could include him — astrology. After that we talked about various games we’d played as children — such as Thomas the Tank Engine, and about becoming artists in Portland. I got the feeling Robin wanted to remind me of the connection we had, and didn’t seem to like that Sarah and I seemed to be hitting it off without him.

When it became dark enough that we had trouble seeing, we returned to my house and, as it often seemed to, the subject of online dating came up. I hadn’t met any other girls who were familiar to the site, so I asked her some basic questions about her use of it, and she told me that she didn’t really need to message anyone since she got about five messages per day and Robin and I (but secretly) were surprised, both thinking that, being an attractive girl, she had to receive more.

It was hard to compare as I’d become accustomed to sending first messages to anyone who looked remotely appealing, but I couldn’t remember getting that many messages. In the time we’d been talking, Robin and Sarah had converged on the couch in our living room, while I pulled my black rolly chair over so I was seated in front of them.

I began to feel like a therapist as the topic of their relationship came up and I crossed my legs and pursed my lips. It seemed an unresolved quandary in both of their minds. They’d gone to a mountain together the night before and had worked out that they wanted a relationship after all, even though in the past Sarah hadn’t completely been on board for monogamy, and then Robin had done something to, well anyway, they were trying to figure out what label to have.

As they talked, they settled comfortably into lying next to each other, and I maintained my role, asking pertinent questions, but mostly just listening and making sure they each had a chance to speak. I made sure that they both got their voice heard, while staying as unbiased as possible, which was pretty unbiased since I couldn’t really figure any opinion to have about the situation.

I wasn’t clear on the exact particular reason why Sarah would choose Robin in the first place, and that may have been a missing link in trying to figure out what should go on in the future. At any rate, after they both had a chance to talk, they seemed to have resolved something, and I hurriedly got back to tinder so I could find a date to match their level of cuddliness.

I arranged for a Mr. Blake Bamford to come over and he asked if I wanted him to pick anything up on the way, so I said a small can of beer. When he arrived, I went out to meet him in his car and it emerged that he had for some reason chosen to wear different shades of fluorescent clothing.

I wondered if I should discreetly ask if he had just come from, or was planning on going to, a rave, but thought better of it and simply ushered him inside my house. I introduced him to everyone and, as you might imagine, awkwardness ensued. dates.name: Charlie & George
dates.dek: After midnight, a new-looking Prius.

spans.t: It was already after midnight when my best male friend from college, and his roommate pulled up in a new looking prius. I was nervous, had anxiously anticipated their arrival; they were passing through on a road trip and I literally jumped into my friend’s arms to keep the score even, he passed me to George, who seemed to have slight difficulty supporting my weight.

I stalled inviting them inside, hoping I would see my previous guest slip out the front door, but no such luck. We arrived to find him still standing in the kitchen and I muttered some explanation. Charlie, always infinitely polite, made conversation, and then told me he seemed nice. After this, I guided them towards my favorite all night coffee house.

My luck was testing me for who should we meet, lingering in the doorway, blocking our entrance, but Jake. Jake whose bed I’d shared only a week earlier. He was wearing an all white jumpsuit and brandishing a power drill menacingly, and told Charlie that he’d been stealing construction tools like drills from somewhere nearby..

I pretended I’d never met him before. We went inside and played a game with frogs and I paid for Charlie’s drink. I got a mango smoothie. then we went to Matthew’s house and sat on the couch for a bit until he came up and told us to get the fuck out with a bare chest and then we walked around outside and talked about tinder and George said the best line for his profile was “kill me” after trying a number of them and Charlie talked about the short person complex.

We arranged where to sleep and Charlie asked me if we could all sleep in the same bed — I offered them all the options — that they could sleep on the couch in the living room, or in my bed with me and they chose bed and Charlie wanted to know if he could sleep with his head next to me instead of his feet (?) and I said yes.

Then we all changed into our pajamas and played a game where we had to list experiences falling under a particular category to each other. Then we went to sleep and first he had his back to me and then he did not and then in the middle of the night when we were both sleeping we, and it was very hot, seemed to put our legs together.

Who cares what happened the next day — it doesn’t matter. Charlie and George came and visited me and we did a lot of things. We went to the Gorge on one day and we got doughnuts on the next day and we did a lot of things beside this. We went to the holocaust museum.

I wasn’t sure how to feel I was a terrible tour guide, having only seen the insides of my date’s houses. having not visited many places since I’d been there, We visited the rose garden Charlie and I play fought on the stage, becoming more and more physically aggressive until he eventually picked me up and I screamed and laughed to put me down.

On the one hand, it seemed a tad trite to experience sadness, at this, a place that was created to foster grief. Yet the moment was so truly mine that I adopted a somber expression, and they, I think, wished they were somewhere, anywhere else. We went downtown and watched a skyscraper being built, discussing what it would be like to live in the elevator built to carry wood between floor and ceiling.

As we walked, Charlie brushed into me, I nudged him back. We didn’t acknowledge this was happening but kept the conversation with George going. I fell into him again, the physical contact seeming progressively more intentional. It wasn’t acknowledged. having not visited many places since I’d been there, We visited the rose garden

dates.name: Ryan
dates.dek: Tea from a green teapot with a silver lid.

spans.t: I watched him drink tea out of a green tea pot with a silver lid. He had a laptop that was in a briefcase and papers in piles on the table in front of him. I had just come from the supermarket and was carrying two heavy bags of groceries, which I was struggling with.

I went to rest at a table in front of the southeast grind and made myself a little bowl of cereal with one of their water cups and a spoon to mix the almond milk in. When I glanced back inside, I accidentally made eye contact with a cute red haired boy around my age and then looked away again.

In order to mix the milk into the cereal I’d bought, I would need a vessel. I grabbed one of the plastic cups for water and again accidentally made eye contact. When I went inside I saw a red-haired boy sitting at a table by himself. He had a laptop and a brief case and a mess of papers set out in front of him.

He had a green teapot on the table. I always wondered who drank tea at this place when it was about \$6 for a cup and all it included was hot water and a tea bag. I left my groceries outside as I could see them from the window, and slumped down onto the couch, every now and then staring at the boy with the red hair without either of us saying anything.

His head was behind the tea pot but I could still see his eyes. It seemed he was intermittently stopping what he was doing just to stare at me. Eventually I got up to go home but came back in to put the cup and spoon away I’d used to eat my cereal. It was then that he approached me and said he had to at least talk to the person he’d been staring at for the past hour or so.

Yes! Success. He helped me carry my groceries back to my house and hung around in my room a little while I put them away. He told me he was on his way to two parties and though I’d decided somewhere around that time that he wasn’t quite as interesting as his blue eyes had at first suggested, I agreed to accompany him on his evening out, interested in a change of scenery.

We walked back to the grind together where it was revealed that unlike me who got everywhere on foot, he actually had a car. It wasn’t a great car — it was old and kind of small and probably a whitish brown color. The backseat, like his table, was piled high with paperwork. On the way we chatted about this and that — what I did for a living and what he did.

The first party was at a beautiful house where everyone was quite friendly. Everyone assumed I was his girlfriend and we had a strange time explaining that we’d met just an hour earlier at a coffee shop. Ryan went off to sit on the counter in the kitchen and drink beer with his friend who he had not seen in a long time and I joined the rest of the party where they were in the middle of explaining a strange game which involved many different-colored plastic pyramids which could be stacked on top of each other to win the game.

Although it looked fun, the rules were inexcusably complex and the objective seemed like an afterthought. More and more people were joining our table and needed the rules to be explained again and again. It emerged that one small gray triangle was missing, and that we had gotten most of the rules wrong. Claire, thin and waifish who was steering the game had a special smile as if to say “we would never play monopoly.” and her partner Brandon, seemed used to following her lead, and only a bit like there was something wrong with his brain that his attractiveness was making up for.

He had a crew cut to match his sad blue eyes. Claire and I were similarly enthusiastic about anything and everything — whether it made sense to be or not. Ryan and I had to go — there was another party his main best friend’s birthday at a restaurant in downtown — but not before I mentioned to Claire that I was looking for a job and Claire told me to apply at a summer camp for especially intelligent children who wanted to use their summer to sew and to program computers.

I jotted down my contact details and we left to drive 15 miles across town; all the while he was explaining his weed business to me. I think I somehow managed to give him the impression that I was both impressed and interested so that’s what we talked about when we stopped at lights. It was very dark and there were lots of winding roads.

I couldn’t be sure I’d ever been to this part of Portland even during the day. After he had built up the party so much, saying how it was his very best friend so he couldn’t miss it, no one was really paying any attention to us. we were sitting on the end away from his friend.

We were playing Never Have I Ever which someone had apparently taken the time to make into an actual board game version with cards and stuff. Except no one seemed to have done anything that the cards said and everyone had these nervous smiles like they were trying not to let anyone into their thoughts.

We agreed that we were both hungry and decided to leave and get crepes. We walked to a crepe place and talked about the part of town we were in. We ordered a banana Nutella crepe to share and discussed what it meant to date and variations to the norm concept like dating multiple people or dating people of the same gender.

He addressed the topic as though I might not have considered it before, strangely, and seemed to be informing me of alternatives to a way of thinking I had not expressed explicitly. I suppose he lumped me in with mainstream opinions. It reminded me a little of how my first boyfriend liked to tell me about things he knew and thought I didn’t.

When the check came (about \$7.50 for the crepe we’d shared), he eyed me mischievously, and asked me conspiratorially if I wanted to put what I had just learned from him to the test. So we split the check. Then we drove to his house, which seemed a bit on the outskirts of town. Instead of a mattress, he simply had lots of pillows and blankets bunched together on the floor (he said he’d just moved in).

My eyes glanced around his room; there was a bookshelf with many unknown treasures. The floor was pleasant hardwood, and seemed clean (he had just moved in). Then we went into the kitchen and he stood in front of the cabinet while I sat on the counter while we talked about the different kinds of tea he had and I told him I didn’t really like tea.

He got two mugs and boiled water and put the bags in those little metal steeping ball things. I think I picked chamomile. We laid on the couch together for a while with his head on my lap (he asked if it was ok to put it there) and then went into his room and he told me I could pick out a big shirt from his closet to wear to bed and made a point of closing his eyes while I changed in the space between his closet and his “bed” which was just a pile of blankets on the floor.

His room was sparse and it had lots of CDs and small things on the wall. He had a bit of weed paraphernalia on it too, and a tan bookshelf with a lot of books in it. We told each other stories as we were falling asleep and in the morning he woke up early and left the room and then he came back so we could cuddle.

In the morning, he asked if I wanted to come grocery shopping with him and he drove us even farther out of town, to a Korean Grocery Store he apparently frequented, and he bought things that I’d never heard of — various kinds of noodles, and seaweed, and I looked for those jelly cup things my mom used to buy my brother and I, hoping to reminisce about how we’d smush them out into our mouths as young children.

Then he drove me back to the place we’d started — my little blue house where my two roommates were chatting amiably on the couch. Though we’d now spent almost 24 hours together, I invited him inside. He said he hadn’t considered coming inside but that now he was here he might as well. My roommates were both there when we got in and I sat at the chair at the table while he sat on the couch and my roommate lay at the other end.

We told them what we had done on our date. It turned out he had helped my roommate book a show a long time ago. He returned a minute after he left because he’d forgotten to get my number and kissed me (for the first time) on the lips behind the curtain that closed off the kitchen so my roommates didn’t see.

After he left, both of my roommates told me that they liked him and that I should invest in him. They said he was attractive. Alpha said that we seemed to have some chemistry. Later that week, Greg told me I should stop going on dates with other people and just try to go out with him again.

I didn’t have my phone so I couldn’t text him until Thursday when I went to retrieve it from David’s house and then I texted him excitedly except he only replied in one word answers so I gave up. I called him when I decided to take the job I’d been offered at the party he took me to and he called me back about a week later but didn’t return my call after that.

I ran into him a long time after that when I was walking towards a library with Westley and he walked in the opposite direction as soon as I saw him but when I made eye contact and casually said hi to him he said hi back.

I can’t quite rank up the strangeness of the dates I’ve been on but this might be #1 out of a small number, yet. But I already know I’m a strange attractor.

I’m unsure of the ratio on the site but the men vastly outnumber the ladies, I’m fairly certain. So it came to my surprise when a woman messaged me saying I looked interesting but how could she be certain? So I assured her I was who I am and exchanged some messages — soon enough I asked her if she would go out for coffee with me and she replied yes: either sometime later in the year or at 4 AM next week.

Pfft. All I could think was why not? I wasn’t all that worried about having my organs harvested and where do you get coffee at 4 AM anyway? So I asked where and there is a place, yay verily, there is a place. So fast forwards to the day or late night we finally set upon and eventually the texts start volleying around 1 AM when I learn she’s at a bar and needs a ride.

So with a hop-skip and a-do I arrive to meet her. She’s at least sober which was different than another person/place but she told me she had been up for over 24 hours, which as I was already asking — tweaker? Poker face already engaged we had a nice chat at the bar for awhile, her asking about my life, what I do, how’s my luck with dating online, pleasant stuff and we shared a few things in common.

She did seem quite out of it, bobbing her head to the music, scribbling on a napkin, asking pretty personal questions, but fine, I just wanted to get to know someone, and that’s what I was doing. I didn’t want to drink all night and neither did she so we decided to go to the 24 hour coffee place she likes.

That’s where things get strange. Soon as we mosey up to order coffee one of her old daters was already there to greet us. A regular 2 AM coffee addict no doubt. She told me he was a past date and they talk before ordering and me and him just exchange funny glances. A couple more awkward moments later I have my cup of java and we go to sit down.

The past dater joins us for a bit but he got tired of standing and listening to my tired mind babbling for my date. A victory I’d take but it wouldn’t last. My babbling continues and I at least have her laughing — at me or with me it didn’t matter. Either way I had an attractive audience and things don’t matter at 2 in the morning after being up all day prior.

She’s a master of Socratic dialogue. She would pretend to know less than she let on and smirk at my mansplaining. She would ask questions of some of the stupid things I said and trip me up. But she made it clear she liked me. She asked if I knew where to get cocaine. “No” was my hasty reply.

“No”. I told her I tried it but not how dumb I consider it. All of a sudden look. Here’s a guy walking in she went on two dates with. O.O. Poker face. Emptiness of thought and mind. I’ve prepared for stupid stuff like this dammit. Sometime later in our conversation I told her how nice it is to suffer from depersonalization at times.

She gets a call. A guy she dated last week wants to meet her and he’s already on his way. Fine I tell her. Fine I don’t care. She tells me she wants to get six of the smartest men she meets online and take them on a bus out into the wilderness where they will learn how to be better people.

What’s this called I ask? “Imagination Land” she tells me. Is there a walled compound involved? No, there’s a castle. I think I must have slipped into that special 3 AM place which madmen witness on occasion. I felt alarmingly at home there. Her other date cruises up on his long board and we go outside to meet him and his nice dog Hero.

Hero was probably the greatest thing of that night. I’ve always liked dogs. Anyway we shake hands and make introductions. I share his joint and fight rising nausea. He tells me he’s on acid, works at a marijuana dispensary, and studies English in college and then starts singing in German. I am an outside observer to the situation I find myself in I tell myself.

And to make this long story shorter we four including Hero went back to her place and hung out on her bed where she invited us to live with her for the next two days and dress us up in her cloths. I hugged and said my goodbyes not too long after. Haven’t seen her since.
