dates.name: Devin
dates.dek: I came to his party with another date.

spans.t: He invited me to a party at his house after we both flaked on dinner at a Mexican restaurant and I responded a week later (the day of the party) that I was on my way and bringing another date. The address he’d given me I realized once I started walking was devoid of a street — in fact, it was only numbers.

So I called him to confirm, my other date waiting politely on the grass where we were resting. He sounded surprisingly chill: not nervous and like he was having a pretty good time. The second thing he said on the phone was that he’d just made a cup of mushroom tea and was about to drink it.

After a thorough sun burning and me promising catboy that you could bring a date to another date if the other date was actually a party (“parties have lots of people”) we arrived at his house to three or so girls lounging on their “slip n’ slide” (was like three feet long, definitely for babies) in almost no clothing.

My date was not in sight and nobody knew who the fuck me and my other date were. We went through the driveway to the side yard. Ironically, the party was like a middle school party in that the boys were playing beer pong and the girls were on the slip n’ slide and they were apparently not drunk enough to interact.

The first thing that happened to me, even before I met the person I was supposed to meet, was this one boy who I would call a basic boy, asked me how old I was. I replied 22 and he acted very suspicious. He then said he could see my nipples and reached out and grabbed one.

I was in a good mood cause of the sun so my admonishment was not nearly enough to teach him a lesson. (Later he told me and his roommate that he’d slept with over 200 girls and we speculated how the nipple grabbing might have evolved into intercourse so many times). My date came out of the house.

He was extremely skinny and had messy platinum blonde hair. He was shirtless, wearing a black bathing suit. He was very white and you could see his nipples too. We sat down to talk with my other date at the head of the table and he and I across from each other. When I say sat down to talk, I mean that a time lapse of the scene might have caught him sitting across from me a few times.

He got up every three minutes to meander into the yard. The conversation came to me getting kicked out of school and he and his roommate got excited and gathered to hear the answer. When I told them, they both seemed nonplussed. “That’s it?” said my date and the other boy wandered away. “I was expecting something crazy.”

Catboy made very little conversation while I talked to mushroom boy and I helped myself to a solo cup half filled with vodka. Catboy was handling the situation well considering no one was talking to him but he told me when mushroom boy had wandered off that he needed to get a haircut. I asked someone if they had scissors and argued with him for a good 15 minutes about whether I would be allowed to cut his hair.

I told him I had a lot of experience with hair cutting though I’d only done it once before and he just wanted it buzzed. I have a feeling Catboy and I looked like we were in middle school compared to the other people there and they mostly left us alone as we had the argument.

After he left, I didn’t talk to anyone for a while. Because of their misunderstanding about my age and probably why I’d brought someone to the party, I anticipated it requiring extreme effort to convince people I was worthy of their time at this particular party. Finally this woman came to my table and I started asking about her shoes.

She was the kind of person who is happy to do all the talking and she started regaling me, and then this older guy with scratchy-looking hair and a baseball cap with stories that often seemed to lack a moral or clear catalyst for telling them. My date came back a few times after a long stint in the house and started talking to me again.

He apologized for flaking on our other date and I argued that I’d been the one to flake. I could feel him holding more power than me and I was not used to it with boys on tinder. As it was happening, I settled for philosophizing about the dynamics of why this happens in different situations and hoping that if I paid less and less attention to him that it would change.

Instead I found myself making an extra effort to be interesting and witty. He continued to talk to me sporadically and also mingle with the other people at the party. By the time Cat Boy got back I had finished my solo cup with vodka in it and had now had like three or four beers in addition.

I led him by the hand to the swing set and tried to make out with him. He did not kiss me back and after a few minutes, got up and sat with a group of people that were in a circle in front of a small fire pit. My tinder date invited me to play beer pong against this tattooed blonde girl who’d been having everyone take multiple pictures of her so that she could get one in which she wasn’t fat.

You could see most of her body. She and the guy who’d grabbed my nipples were on the other side. My tinder date wasted no opportunity to make fun of me and it wasn’t unwarranted as sober I get approximately 0 points in beer pong usually and at that point I was sloshed. But I was too drunk to try to be witty and we started actually flirting.

The end of the game was dramatic as we won even though we were doing terribly the whole time and I think it was on account of my skills. He kissed me. He asked if I wanted a tour of the house. I followed him inside. I was so happy to be drunk; I practically never get drunk past the point of being silly and overthinking things.

He showed me the bathroom and the kitchen and then brought me to his bedroom. There was a door in the far corner that I thought was a closet but when he opened it up it was an actual whole extra other room. I found this hilarious and was giggling in the corner or this extra room as he told me about things he’d considered using it for like hiding little people.

Having had very little sleep the night before, as well as being drunk, I fell asleep on the boy’s bed. I presume while I was out like a light, he went out to enjoy the rest of the party. I woke up and the light had changed. I remembered Cat Boy and quickly texted him “hey sooo sorry.

“ He replied “I went home.” I left my phone in my dates room on the dresser and went back to the party but it was basically over. There were about 7 people left and they were all gathered in the living room. I arrived just in time for a long drawn out discussion of what movie to watch.

We decided on “this is the end” and it was going great except this one bitch who had some huge problem with the skinny guy and would repeat “ugh turn it off” every time he came on the screen. She was extremely hot so of course we changed it to this weird movie about old men having boring conversations over drinks until one of them goes into the bathroom and gets beat up by a robot.

It didn’t really matter at that point, no one was watching. We retired to the kitchen and I don’t remember almost any of the conversation we had over one more beer. While the movie night had turned back into talk night, and by the sounds of it, there was some drunken debauchery occurring, I joined Devin’s roommate at the table that held the remaining alcohol and we speculated, as I mentioned, the legitimacy of the number nipple grabber had quoted us as to how many women he’d slept with.

Not only that, but considered how the nipple grabbing might have contributed to that number. I went upstairs and fell asleep comfortably next to my tinder date only to wake up like three hours later when he left for work the next day. He was a pizza delivery boy I think? I couldn’t go back to sleep.

I felt inextricably happy for no reason at all I guess because I like waking up in strange places. I called this one boy I’d been talking to on OkCupid for a while and we had a magnificent phone conversation, really the best, in which he told me how many people he’d slept with, and then we did the math together to figure out if that was a lot, considering how it would be stretched out into all the years he’d been alive.

Then I called David. He explained that he’d waited an hour after I apparently left the party with another boy and never came back. I didn’t understand as the last I’d seen of him, he’d gone to join some other party-goers by a fire pit. But he told me after he’d seen us kiss before going inside, that “all his conversation had left him.”

Poetic most definitely and I found myself staggering behind the force of what — no! it couldn’t be — were actual feelings?! The conversation got progressively hairier. What started as innocent denial and ahrigin off on my part became a succession of apologies and finally crying “no I actually really like you.” insistently, to a dead silence on the other end.

He explained that he could no longer trust me and that he’d consider whether he could be friends with me. After that conversation I called some random people on my phone to unload what had just happened. One of them I realized, as I was about to hit “call,” was another date and I stopped in my tracks before unloading what had just happened onto him.

This whole feelings thing was getting to be a bit too much for me, and nausea that had been suspiciously absent the night before formed in my stomach. I got some coconut water from the fridge downstairs and started to feel much better. I climbed into bed with my date’s roommate, who had started to feel like a friend, and he let me interrupt him and change topics as much as I wanted.

I arranged a meet up with someone who I’d been texting late at night for a few months now, and my new friend, who happened to be headed in a similar direction, walked me to a somewhat sophisticated brunch place on hawthorne. I could see lots of people were drinking mimosas in tall flutes through the glass window and grabbed a table by myself, while my date was ostensibly still in transit.

I tried to show him to another date: Gabriel, only to find that he’d unmatched me. In the end I stole his sweatshirt. It’s black and has razor blades on it. I wear it a lot considering the zippers broken. But it’s really cool — like I said — it has razor blades on it.

dates.name: Pavel
dates.dek: The waiters thought I’d been stood up.

spans.t: After about five minutes, he still hadn’t arrived and I began picking up and putting down my coffee (because it was too hot) and pretending I couldn’t tell that all the waiters who passed by me each like five times felt bad because they thought I’d been stood up. He texted me that he was there but was too shy to actually come inside…so I went outside to meet him.

He hated the breakfast place or it was way too fancy. He by the way was very skinny, with shiny brown hair running down his back, had a pretty face, and was wearing all black. We moved outside. We shared a mushroom and goat cheese omelette which was delicious but less delicious than the beautiful day we were seeing walk by us.

He told me a story about his ex-girlfriend, who had been into Bondage. Upon her request, he had done things like slap her, and spit in her mouth, but did not like doing these things, and I could see the discomfort stretch across his face as he discussed this with me. We tried to split it evenly, but he paid because I realized I didn’t have enough.

After that we walked amiably to my house, except that he didn’t talk very much and I became a nervous Nancy, beginning thoughts and then deeming them not interesting enough to continue. We weren’t even walking at the same pace. On the way we picked up a tiny dictionary from a garage sale, and We arrived at my house and where I stayed in bed after he left, basically starving.

When we got there, we settled into my bed which was, really, the only place to hang out in my room, and looked through men I’d been messaging with on tinder. He started messaging one of them nonsense about muscle milk and rather than actually having sex, we proceeded to sort of moan and make sex noises, bashing each other lightly in the chest.

Eventually he left as the sun was going down and I crawled back into my bed, knowing there was nothing to eat in the house except some stale cereal, and feeling empty, drained, and to be honest, a bit depressed. Perhaps it was the hangover finally catching up with me, (though I didn’t feel sick or have a headache), but more likely it was the way the darkness had slowly crawled in through the windows, interrupting my peaceful day, and reminding me that, despite having seen so very many people that day and the previous, I was still, now, very much alone.

Despite my better judgment, I returned once again, to the only friend I really had, OkCupid itself, and messaged someone, convincing them to meet me even at this late hour, with the promise that they could sleep over if they couldn’t find transportation home this late at night. My last resort was his kismet, as he explained he hadn’t checked his okcupid in over a month and had somehow opened it to find my message immediately.

He started messaging one of them nonsense about muscle milk and rather than actually having sex, we proceeded to sort of moan and make sex noises, bashing each other lightly in the chest.

Eventually he left as the sun was going down and I crawled back into my bed, knowing there was nothing to eat in the house except some stale cereal, and feeling empty, drained, and to be honest, a bit depressed. Perhaps it was the hangover finally catching up with me, (though I didn’t feel sick or have a headache), but more likely it was the way the darkness had slowly crawled in through the windows, interrupting my peaceful day, and reminding me that, despite having seen so very many people that day and the previous, I was still, now, very much alone.

Despite my better judgment, I returned once again, to the only friend I really had, OkCupid itself, and messaged someone, convincing them to meet me even at this late hour, with the promise that they could sleep over if they couldn’t find transportation home this late at night.
My last resort was his kismet, as he explained he hadn’t checked his okcupid in over a month and had somehow opened it to find my message immediately.

dates.name: Michael Mount
dates.dek: Mostly I remember the bus.

spans.t: What I most remember from this date is being on the bus. It was a long bus trip and I had to make a transfer at night in a place I’d never been before. Usually I don’t mind being out at night alone but something about waiting for a bus is the most maddening thing.

Because it doesn’t come, and you’ve just been sitting there that whole time, who’s to say you’re not crazy for imagining you could predict when a 20 ton vehicle would swoop you up out of the blue in the middle of the night and take you precisely where you wanted to go. My brother had set up a play date with a guy he knew from college.

I couldn’t quite believe that someone so incredibly good looking would want to be my brother’s friend, who I knew as nerdy As it turned out, we had another date joining us that night, and he made it clear that ours was the date and not Michael’s as he quickly slipped the bartender a \$20 and said he was paying for my drink too.

It was our little secret, though surely Jon would’ve mentioned we’d come here together before. We brought the beers..I imagined for a second that I didn’t know him previously, that we’d just happened to meet, and because we’d gone to the bar together, and he liked me, he’d decided to pay for my drink. We didn’t discuss our previous meetings but he slipped me a quick smile at the same time as he slipped the bartender the bill.

I don’t quite remember what we talked about on the date. I know we played a game called cuthroat which is meant for three people but to be honest, is the clumsiest game I could imagine. I wasn’t really in the running but I would clumsily take my shots anyway, preparing the motion of my hands like a ritual and wondering what it was they could value so much about being able to shoot a ball into a tiny pocket.

I didn’t understand it. On the sidelines, I talked to Michael about his book, which was an expose on a fictional narcissist. I was surprised that he’d written a whole book, and that he was talking about it so nonchalantly. Afterwards I went home with Jon Storch and didn’t see Michael Mount again. Jon and I didn’t have sex that night, instead I told him awkwardly that I thought we were better off as friends, assuming he would agree as he hand’t indicated he’d like to date me.

Thereafter we settled into an uncomfortable silence which ended with us spooning our way to sleep. In fact, Jon had mentioned his frequent tuesday night games with the legendary michael on our first date, which happened to be at the exact place he’d suggested. I played along, texting both people who evidently hadn’t discussed that Jon already knew me.

dates.name: Xander
dates.dek: He mansplained me feminism.

spans.t: He mansplained me feminism It was late when I set this date with a delivery man and I was video chatting with my mother on the giant monitor in the living room that wasn’t mine but my roommates. My mother wanted to meet my date who arrived: tall, and in a leather jacket. There was a bar only a few blocks from my house that I rarely frequented, despite its proximity.

There was a park on the other side of it. We ordered drinks for ourselves and chose a high two person table overlooking the park. It seemed we had a lot in common as we’d both studied the same subject in college but rather than compare our experiences he used this — the fact that I was supposedly interested in the subject — as a launchpad to tell me all about his experience, including things I’d learned in my intro class.

Blech. I was bored. In spite of myself I could not figure out how a situation that had seemed so promising — he was tall, attractive and dorky to boot, we were getting beers at a bar near my house — had suddenly turned into an opportunity to explain every detail of a class trip he’d gone on with his hilarious trip leader Ralph, master of hijinx…even so I listened on, unsure how to politely steer the conversation away from this veritable hell.

Afterwards we walked around nearby. It was dark and late and a little bit spooky at night. We’d arrived at another park, or perhaps the same one from the other side when he decided to explain his policies regarding feminism. “Women are always getting hit on by guys when they don’t want to be. Honestly, I feel bad for them.

They could just be enjoying a day at the park, sitting alone reading, and suddenly there’s a swarm of guys who think it’s their personal business…” I supposed this was true but hoped to interject a bit more nuance to the situation. To be honest, this hadn’t happened to me very often, and I for one loved talking to strangers.

I felt a bit sorry that he was recounting an experience I hadn’t had for me and wished he would only give a little bit of my opinion that I might convince him this wasn’t supremely true. In a sense I felt that what he was saying was that women couldn’t quite handle themselves in public; they weren’t equipped to say no to guys that wanted their number, and he felt sorry for the poor dears who had to field off requests from men like a spartan in a cage of lions. as when I tried to speak, he sort of talked over me.

He just couldn’t seem to get past this one-sided picture of the woman minding her own business, say in the park or a public library, when suddenly, from out of nowhere, not 2 but three or four men attack her with their kind words and compliments, refusing to take no for an answer. Now I consider myself a fairly attractive girl but this has never been my experience.

Sure I’ve been asked out by the odd man or two but never a tall good looking guy like himself. In spite of himself, I felt like advising him to try just once or twice, for the sake of the women in my neighborhood, sitting alone in the park, waiting for someone too….I tried to make the point I felt like saying: “if she’s sitting in the park reading, she probably wants to be asked out.

If she didn’t want to, she could just stay home by herself.” I gave up on trying to say anything, realizing he’d literally just mansplained feminism to me After this he came home and he didn’t want to stay over. This was an undeniably strange turn of events. I couldn’t tell if he thought I didn’t want him to stay.

In any event, he put on one last youtube video which was the theme song to the show “too many cooks” which, if you haven’t seen it, goes on and on. At this point I was so done with the date that I simply told him enough was enough and that I hadn’t bargained for this hour and a half long video.
He left shortly after and we didn’t speak again.

dates.name: Paul
dates.dek: After the sixth long phone call with Tyler.

spans.t: After my sixth long phone conversation with Tyler, I called one of my potential dates that I’d neglected to follow up on after they’d texted me after I’d given them my number in hopes that we could talk on the phone. He told me that he’d just gotten home from watching a movie by himself and that before that he’d gone to the park and swung on the swings by himself.

We talked about online dating and he said for him it was sad and disappointing and we agreed that meeting after messaging online took the spontaneity out of meeting potential partners. He said he’d gone one a few dates and they’d all gone horrendously bad or the people had been boring and he had or hadn’t followed up with them, that sometimes he’d followed up with them only because he wanted friends to hang out with because he was bored.

He lived with two boys – his brothers, and they were all in a band together. He’d spent the day in the recording studio. I told him that he and his brothers were probably secretly the Jonas Brothers. He said the movie he’d seen had been a chick flick but that he’d liked it a lot and that it made him feel something and that people liked movies that made them feel things.

He said that he often watched movies by himself and though it seemed like an undesirable situation, he enjoyed spending time by himself a lot. He said his brothers had moved to Portland after he’d left home and I said that he was secretly Nick Jonas from the Jonas Brothers and why hadn’t he told me that before, when we’d been talking on the dating website.

We decided to meet the next day for me to give him the art lesson. He came the next day after 4:00 and we sat down at the wooden table and I was all frantic and upset after having had nothing to eat the entire day. I was talking a lot and fast it seemed and I was trying to calm myself down but I felt I had low energy and low ability to be pleasant and calm since I was food deprived.

I had planned a lesson for him based on the book “Drawing on The right Side of the Brain” by Betty Edwards so I gave him the shell to draw and he described its surface as I asked him to do and then he took down the details on the paper. I was impressed with how much he’d captured and he said he felt that it was a very poor attempt.

I said it wasn’t fair for him to degrade his own performance like that, and that I was being genuine in saying that it was good. I was a little jealous, even, since he’d had so little training. I lectured him about observing things carefully and how you were supposed to do something and how art wasn’t about the finished product but about altering your vision.

I had him draw a gesture of me with my head on the table; the pose was inspired by feeling dead. His drawing was very good and he drew my hair and the lower half of my body and everything and it was scribbly and squiggly and once again I tried to convince him that it really was an excellent work of art.

He did a contour drawing of something else without looking. After we had done everything, he drew a maze that was born out of a drawing of my phone that I’d been holding. Then he went back and labelled all the drawings and drew himself being abducted by a flying saucer in his first shell drawing and added some flowers to the maze one and added captions and titles to all of them.

I felt like I was not standing on anything, I had no idea where to go with the art lesson, he refused to acknowledge his talent and I had not been prepared for him to already understand the basis of conceptual art and felt strange about shifting gears after I’d provided this basis of a solid foundation for our lesson based on the assumption that people were all dumb and didn’t know anything and couldn’t think for themselves.

I felt that I’d failed myself by not teaching him what he wanted to know and he seemed to be frustrated or at least tuned out of our date. I took some pictures of him with his drawings and he told me I should keep them and that I could send him pictures of them.

He said he was going to a show that was nearby and I asked if I could come if I finished my game night early and he didn’t seem especially enthusiastic about me coming but we figured out where it was together anyway on his map on his phone and he played trying to guess where the venue was (it was at a pizza place?) without typing in the address on google maps but gave up and typed it in anyway and it was where he had just gotten to with moving his finger along the roads.

I promised him I’d send him pictures of his drawings. He told me a bit about the place that he worked and I apologized for making him come all the way to my house for the short art lesson. His coworker had texted him that she had forgotten her keys and she needed to close the shop and so he had to drive back to where he worked and give her the keys.

Right before he stood up to leave, he said “Would you like to get a beer sometime?” and I couldn’t tell if his strange voice when he said that was because he was nervous about what I would say or because he didn’t necessarily actually want to or something completely different. I agreed excitedly as I hadn’t been sure that this date was going well at all, and especially not wanting to ruin my near perfect streak, and he left.

I neglected to text him the pictures and instead sent him a message saying “I never sent you the pictures” and then a wall of a few dozen emojis which he completely ignored. (We talked on the phone the night before about how he’d gone to a movie by himself and playing music in a band and he agreed to come over for an art lesson.

The next day I didn’t eat at all and then I was starving when he got there which made it hard to communicate or behave positively or concentrate on the impression I might be giving him in any regard. We sat at the table in the living room and I showed him how to do certain things with his pencil or he showed me since he was unequivocally better at drawing than me even though he’d never tried.)

dates.name: Connor
dates.dek: Delightfully celebratory of my drinking.

spans.t: We talked on the phone earlier that day and he appeared to be delightfully celebratory of my inclination towards becoming an alcoholic. We met up that evening, he picked me up at my house and I encouraged him to hang out in my room for a short period of time while I “got dressed.” I had procrastinated taking a shower for a while and had just put on overalls without a shirt when he called to say he’d arrived.

I went to his car, which was black and stubby, maybe a Prius or a BMW, but it was shiny. I decided not to change afterall and wore my black overalls on the date in which we went to this bar he’d told me about which was supposed to be hilarious since it had its name repeated a bunch of times.

The bar seemed like a regular old dive bar, but with straw on the floor. I don’t remember most of what we talked about but, as always, we settled on my favorite subject (online dating). He told me a little bit about some girl he’d been seeing from okcupid and how they’d ended up making out on some swings the night before and that he was gonna go on another date with her, but said that I was much more interesting and that she wasn’t very good at small talk or that they were still making small talk after going on two dates.

I told him all this other random stuff about me and my OkCupid life. He said that he doesn’t like it when girls give ultimatums on their profile like “If you’re 40, don’t even think about messaging me.” I had the idea that my profile had some things that were similar to that so I questioned him further about what he didn’t like about that.

Anyway, I bought us shots and beers I think and we drank them, and I kind of remember becoming relatively intoxicated, also the night included my going up to the bar by myself and ordering an entire plate of onion rings which I devoured singled handedly (I’m not sure I’d eaten anything that day), and which he commented that he liked how I ate them with my hands not caring etc.

I didn’t feel like he had the right to judge me for any of the things and was disappointed as on the phone he’d presented himself to me as someone who could understand my sense of humor and had a similar one, which I took to mean he might be relatively confident and unabashed at doing “weird” things, rather than the type to point them out as examples of model behavior.
He dropped me off at my house in his black car after only a few hours (it was like 11) I think he had to do something the next day, and we agreed to hang out in the future (though we didn’t).

dates.name: Jasper
dates.dek: A friend from the Rocky Horror crowd, two a.m.

spans.t: I made a friend in the crowd that streamed out of the Rocky Horror Picture Show when it ended at the ungodly hour of two am. He led me back to one of his friend’s houses, where we proceeded to drink and talk, with the constant presence of a large gray bulldog, who probably weighed more than me and was, to be honest, making me very nervous.

The two friends I had made left abruptly and I was left in the house of this stranger, and his dog, but rather than asking me to leave, he seemed complacently friendly, perhaps happy to have the company, certainly excited to have a willing audience for his impromptu obedience class; he told me to grip the ears and if the dog didn’t listen to me, to climb on top of it and hold its ears down to show it who was boss.

I didn’t really feel like doing that right then, I wasn’t in a bossy mood, but I was intimidated by Jasper and the prospect of staying at his house even though I didn’t know him so I tried my best to follow his instructions. But I sort of just wanted to make friends with the dog and to have Jasper teach him discipline.

He was curiously invested in my progress and assumed that I was similarly invested. We went upstairs with the dog who I had begun calling “Kitty,” and I sat in his black leather chair that was directly in front of a massive stereo system as he played different records and cds. We eventually got tired and smoked weed and decided we should go to bed if we planned on getting food with his friends in the morning.

I was having all sorts of anxious but interesting thoughts, having gotten high for the first time in so long and was engrossed in them, was thinking something magical as I sat there in the black chair, was analyzing every aspect of my interaction with him, whether to make eye contact etc. Even though I was barely talking; I asked him about some of the records he’d put on, feigning a bit more knowledge of music then I really had.

He said that he worked in sound and often went record shopping and had found the records but had yet to listen to them even though he’d bought them a long time ago. We went to bed and the dog fell asleep right in between us, though we were just barely touching hands as we drifted off.

In the morning we went to a few different places, we walked around, we got coffee, we went to my house, we went to a bar that he frequents, my feet were tired from walking and my shoes were pretty uncomfortable, they were the Harley Davidson motorcycle boots and I wasn’t wearing socks. The strangest thing that happened perhaps was when we got back to my house.

Ostensibly, this would be my time to say goodbye, seeing as I had a house, and I’d been staying at his only out of convenience. Instead, this was not even mentioned. It’s unclear whether the thought of leaving me home did not occur to him; instead it remained one of many errands, no different than the rest.

It seemed I belonged with him, not in any dramatic sort of way, only in the way of camaraderie between two people who have suddenly come to share a living situation. There was no comment. The dog came with us of course and a lot of our interaction was based on talking to the dog, or him telling me about it.

I asked him questions about it. I reflected on my overwhelming desire in this situation for this interaction to be pleasant and devoid of negative feelings, which was resulting in my not talking about myself at all, not disclosing much of my personality whatsoever, and listening with feigned enthusiasm, to whatever it occurred to him to tell me.

I was also intent, perhaps, on continuing this strange encounter for as long as it might go on for. There was no end in sight. I felt any hint of my personhood might alert him to the fact that he was now harboring a second person. No, the safest way was to remain faceless, nameless, boring, uninteresting, numb.

The male’s wife was wearing, I think, a very elegant sun hat and they started taking pictures in front of this guy’s jeep that had parked right in front of us except the wheels were huge so maybe it was actually a monster truck.

He and his sister swapped clothes and texted a picture of them to their mother. I couldn’t understand the relationship between the sister and the wife completely. We ordered more drinks and there was a whole thing with the bill — the wife was complaining to the waitress that she’d charged too much, the wife was supposed to foot the whole bill, I didn’t understand why, perhaps she’d been treated in the past?

The dynamics of the situation fell through the slats in my tired mind. There was a little questions about how Jasper and I knew each other and some reminiscence about how Jasper and the male knew each other. I felt like Jasper didn’t quite know how to navigate the social situation and I, for one, didn’t either.

He told a few longish stories that were met with an unenthusiastic response. We all walked back to their house and the guy barbequed some stuff in the side yard. Their apartment was very nice, everything was white, it seemed expensive. We went and sat at the picnic table in the back. The wife and sister were engrossed in a conversation and ignored me.

There was something about the food — I wasn’t hungry or it didn’t taste good. The girls were making fun of the boy for keeping on bringing out more and more food even though ostensibly no one was extremely hungry. I got in a conversation with the man and it felt a lot better than the conversations intermittently I’d been having with the two women who reminded me of everyone I’d gone to high school with.

Nevertheless, I enjoyed witnessing their burgeoning female bond and noting the things it seemed to be based on though I felt distinctly that I could not participate in it. Eventually, Jasper and I walked home and after we got home we relaxed and watched a comedy show — Sarah Silverman probably — some girl making lots of semi-funny jokes that I was engrossed in, thinking about women comics etc. and then we finally settled on watching Trainspotting which was great and I’d never seen it before.

We were cuddling on the couch and it was sweet and very cozy even though he seemed to be in a strange position. Eventually we went upstairs and went to bed and made out a little and he ran his hands over my body but didn’t take any of my clothes off. The dog came bounding onto the bed, though, and our excursion ended.

In the morning, we said goodbye on the platform between the stairs, unsure of what sort of closeness had been fostered, and therefore what sort of goodbye might be appropriate. The sun was streaming in through the window above, making the stairs are dappled and sunny. Perhaps he took my hand — I cannot think what happened. and he didn’t seem like he was trying to get rid of me at all, in fact, he seemed a little sad that I was leaving.
I said vaguely that we would see each other again, and perhaps exchanged phone numbers.

Tyler and I talked on the phone for hours before we eventually met up. He told me he loved me in one of his first messages, and told me he needed my number so he could send me a picture of his friend that looked like me. We didn’t meet up right away because he was in the Bay Area, on the last leg of a long trip.

He asked if we could meet when he finally landed in Portland. He told me he’d gone to Princeton and told me that no one really great didn’t go to one of the four best colleges (Harvard, Yale, Stanford) that he was tired of sex. He asked if I’d be disappointed if he didn’t want to have sex with me and I said yes as there was no really good answer to this question and he seemed kind of disappointed in that.

I wasn’t sure I understood, but, as usual, I gave him the benefit of the doubt till I met him in person. He had already asked me everything there was to know about the dates I’d went on and we’d compared numbers of people we’d each slept with. He’d slept with eighty people which I thought was a lot but he pointed out that if I kept up the rate I’d explained to him then I would far surpass him.

He also told me he did not like sex that much anymore and that often it made girls upset when he didn’t want to sleep with them. He asked me if it would make me upset if he didn’t want to sleep with me and I said yes, it would and he was disappointed, I guess he’d thought I was better than that.

He said he only liked to have sex doggie style. He told me he’d been sent to a juvenile delinquent high school after causing a lot of trouble in his elementary school. He said he’d been traveling around recently and since he’d graduated from Princeton. He also said that anybody who didn’t go to Princeton or Stanford or Harvard or Yale was a joke.

He said he knew a lot of the cool people in all the cities he visited and that it was hard to find people you actually thought were cool. He said he thought he knew a lot of them that he saw them whenever he visited New York City. Tyler and I confirmed our date midway through my date with Jasper.

Jasper and I were sitting on a bus bench when he called and it took me a little while to figure out who he was. He was supposed to meet me at Brooklyn Park which is a few blocks from my house. I left Jasper’s house early that morning and traveled to the park. First though I went to my house and probably changed.

I think I wore a punkish outfit perhaps the skeleton shirt with my tight black dress. We were supposed to meet on Monday so I left Jasper’s house in the morning and went to the park where we said we’d meet but he was not there and he said since I hadn’t confirmed, he’d gone back to sleep instead of driving the hour to Portland from the farm he was staying at.

He told me it was my fault for not answering his phone call when he’d called that morning, (my phone had died while staying at Jasper’s and I’d bought a new charger so I could see where he was when he didn’t show up as promised.) I said nothing but that I’d wait for him there, and laid down under the swing to overturn handfuls of wood chips and watch a small child play on the slide. \{\{\{ didn’t take full responsibility for it.

He did come eventfully after I laid on the floor of the park for a while and got beer and paper from the store across the street and some other useless things like a mascara that I never used — I don’t think even once. He was a bit shorter than I’d expected though he was handsome.

One of his eyes was swollen shut. We got in his truck and seemed to be arguing already. We couldn’t figure out where to go to eat and eventually, after driving a little, came back to where we’d started and went to this vegan cafe across the street from the park that I’d never been to even though it was blocks from my house.

We got food after deliberating for a while and agreeing to share a bread and cheese plate and I walked around looking at the unique things they had in what was like a vegan grocery store. I sat down and he came to sit next to me.\}\}\} Eventually he appeared towering over me, though he wasn’t actually very tall, only looked so from my position on the ground.

We got into his truck and he told me he’d been hoping I’d show up in something like a long skirt with flowers on it. About to dip onto the highway, I found we’d gotten into an argument about where we should eat, and we turned back — eventually settling on a cafe that was directly across from the park.

While I wandered around the shop looking at all the little things they also carried such as honey sticks and other bee products, he perused the menu on the wall for what seemed like forever. After a while I got tired of that and went to sit down on a chair with a large base.

When the food finally came, the waitress had made some kind of a mistake. Rather than accepting her apology he burned the point into the ground, making sure I and the waitress knew it was not his fault that his food had come with the wrong type of bun. I was confused as to why he’d kept her at our table for so long, enunciating every detail about the bread that wasn’t the kind he’d wanted, until she eventually was set free and dipped back into her shop.

I asked him whether he was trying to hit on her and he said that no, no, she had not been attractive enough for that. I allowed him to walk me back to my house, which was only a few blocks away, and then we sat next to each other on the couch, he explaining to me that he had thought I might be a little high energy for him when we had our phone calls but that he hoped I would be different in person.

He then told me about his last tinder date which had happened in San Francisco with an Asian girl about my age. He had taken her to a park and then home but he didn’t like her and despite her trying to have sex with him, he had refused and gone to his place. He explained the factors which had led to this decision, one of them being that he was tired.

He said he might have been interested in her had she been more chill and not tried to hook up with him. I suggested that perhaps it was because she was much younger than him that he’d found her annoying and that maybe if he dated girls his own age he’d have more things to talk about and more things in common.

I was very tired, having not slept at my house the night before, and we agreed to take a nap together, agreeing first, also, that it would be just a nap. But as we lapsed into silence, he did not keep his promise, opting instead to try something very sinister. Once I realized what he was doing, I stopped him immediately.

He would not apologize. Rather than bading him adieu, I explained to him over and over again why what he had attempted was unacceptable until finally he apologized and we I think we took the nap we’d been planning. We ended up sitting on the steps outside my building. I had been telling him that he was required, whether or not the rest of our date went well, to send me whatever it was he had previously written about art in the past.

He chose that moment to tell me he was not the age he had said he was on his profile but in fact a very different age — one that was three years older than the one he’d previously claimed to be. He said it matter-of-factly — like all the other things he had said which were essentially confessions, his voice didn’t convey any sense of guilt about the situation.

I asked him why he’d chosen that moment to tell me that, and he said it was because he thought the date was going pretty well. He said he was writing a book about what made art good or bad. I said that whether or not we went on more dates, he was required to share his book with me as that I was pretty sure I’d thought about the topic more than him.

He seemed to be very bored about the whole thing. Again, we disagreed about where we wanted to eat. He said he wanted something different and interesting, like a cafe, and I told him I preferred something more traditional, like a diner, or a nice sit down restaurant. I tried to explain that we could lapse into the pretend versions of ourselves but he was not really listening, or could not understand for some reason.

We settled on a bar that had two sides, one just for eating, which was good because I’d forgotten to bring my ID. He wanted to know all about the situation I’d been in the night before. I had lied to him on the phone and told him I was staying with three lesbian girls.

He tried to figure out if they were having me stay with them because they wanted to get with me and asked me questions to determine this. When I mentioned that he was not telling me much about himself, he explained that he did not feel like talking about himself because he had just been on a trip and had had to explain to everyone what he had been doing and he was tired of it.

I had just come from a weird sort of date that lasted for about three days but I concealed that fact by changing the facts a little bit — saying I’d been staying with three lesbians. He seemed to be trying to figure out whether these fictional women had liked my personality, or whether it had been about them trying to get me to sleep with them.

I had to make up more and more “facts” and details about the situation to appease his strange hunger for an understanding of what had happened there at that house where I had been staying for the past few days. I don’t think his findings were conclusive. When the meal was finished, he did not pay for my half of it.

When I mentioned that he was not telling me much about himself, he explained also to me that, because he had just come from a trip in which he had to explain a bunch of things about his life to a lot of people and therefore a lot of times, he was not in the mood to talk about himself, and was content to simply listen to me talk about myself.

He said this as though my feelings in the situation were very unimportant. I cannot imagine why he expected me to be fine with that, though I waited for a further explanation. Perhaps he considered it an honor for me to get to talk about myself the whole time, however, it wasn’t something that was important to me — it was only something that he was interested in.

He didn’t pay for my meal. Afterwards he wanted to go to the supermarket. I wanted to walk but he needed to take his truck. I walked and he met me there in his truck. We stayed until the store closed and just as it was closing, he sent me on a mission to get something he needed (I think it was butter, but there was some confusion about whether it should be salted or not) while he got something else he needed.

We got back in the car and I suggested different things we could do but he was tired and eventually we just went home and went to sleep in my bed. We woke up early, and I was still very tired, but felt slightly sick at having shared a bed with him. but felt slightly uncomfortable at just having shared a bed with someone I did not like in the slightest.

In the morning, he told me that he only found girls that were younger than him attractive. Once again, we were sitting side by side on my couch, this time as I watched him swipe through girls on okcupid. He had his preferences set to girls exactly 22 years of age. He commented on each one, saying they were either ugly, or that they seemed like a slut.

My roommate overheard him and asked him to explain what he meant. Next he argued to me that none of my friends actually wanted to be friends with me and instead that they just wanted to get into my pants. I convinced him that they weren’t trying to get into my pants, citing that none of them had ever tried, even given ample opportunity.

He changed tacts, and said they were most likely using me for my emotional intelligence — my ability to help them understand themselves better. I didn’t think this was true either, and told him their emotions rarely came up and we mostly made up strange scenarios together, and giggled vaguely about them. As we talked, we moved naturally out into the sun outside.

I finished by saying that I didn’t think I had a superior understanding of emotions, and that they seemed more in touch with their emotions at times. Somehow it ended up that I was lying on the grass outside my house looking up at him, as he claimed, moving away from me while shielding his eyes from the sun, that I had basically surrendered the argument to him because I knew he was right.

I didn’t think that was fair, but I saw now the potential damage to his very fragile ego, were I, inevitably, to prove myself right, so I simply discontinued the argument, and told him that winning an argument against him wasn’t my intention. After all, I was certain I was right, since he didn’t know much about any of the friendships I was referencing.

I told him that I didn’t want to make enough points in order to win the argument but rather I was interested in finding out whether he had any interesting reasoning behind what he was saying and he took that to mean that I had given up. I started to explain how that wasn’t true but felt frustrated and explained that he seemed to be changing the terms of our argument so we went inside.

We decided to take a walk around the block and he told me that I had looked better in my pictures. We discussed what our plans for the day were and he said he wanted to go to Powell’s books and that perhaps I could come with him and help him pick up girls. He described how this would work.

We would arrive together. We would scour the store for prospective women that he would be interested in hitting on and when we found one he would make sure she had seen us together. He explained that the main point of my being with him was to avoid seeming like a predator. Once we had been seen together we would then separate and I would strike up a conversation with her, him in close proximity.

At some point he would join the conversation and if it was going well, I should take the cue and let them finish talking so he could take her home. I told him that I didn’t want to do it if that was the end goal, and that I was maybe interested in making friends with girls if that was going to be the end result, but that I didn’t want to be his wingman, and that the main point of my being there was to prove that he wasn’t a predator, when I could not, in good conscience, support that claim.

We went back to my house and he unwrapped the two large pieces of meat that he’d bought at the supermarket, letting the gamey smell waft through our meatless household, then cooked both of them for himself and left without cleaning the grease from the pan. My roommate was none too pleased when he arrived back home, as I hadn’t noticed this trace of his horrible rudeness in the wake of his departure.
He called me the following Saturday while I was at a party and I simply let it go to voicemail.

While I wandered around the shop looking at all the little things they also carried such as honey sticks and other bee products, he perused the menu on the wall for what seemed like forever. After a while I got tired of that and went to sit down on a chair with a large base.

When the food finally came, the waitress had made some kind of a mistake. Rather than accepting her apology he burned the point into the ground, making sure I and the waitress knew it was not his fault that his food had come with the wrong type of bun.

I was confused as to why he’d kept her at our table for so long, enunciating every detail about the bread that wasn’t the kind he’d wanted, until she eventually was set free and dipped back into her shop. I asked him whether he was trying to hit on her and he said that no, no, she had not been attractive enough for that.

I allowed him to walk me back to my house, which was only a few blocks away, and then we sat next to each other on the couch, he explaining to me that he had thought I might be a little high energy for him when we had our phone calls but that he hoped I would be different in person.

He then told me about his last tinder date which had happened in San Francisco with an Asian girl about my age. He had taken her to a park and then home but he didn't like her and despite her trying to have sex with him, he had refused and gone to his place. He explained the factors which had led to this decision, one of them being that he was tired. He said he might have been interested in her had she been more chill and not tried to hook up with him. I suggested that perhaps it was because she was much younger than him that he'd found her annoying and that maybe if he dated girls his own age he'd have more things to talk about and more things in common.

I was very tired, having not slept at my house the night before, and we agreed to take a nap together, agreeing first, also, that it would be just a nap. But as we lapsed into silence, he did not keep his promise, opting instead to try something very sinister. Once I realized what he was doing, I stopped him immediately. He would not apologize.
Rather than bading him adieu, I explained to him over and over again why what he had attempted was unacceptable until finally he apologized and we I think we took the nap we’d been planning.

We ended up sitting on the steps outside my building. I had been telling him that he was required, whether or not the rest of our date went well, to send me whatever it was he had previously written about art in the past. He chose that moment to tell me he was not the age he had said he was on his profile but in fact a very different age - one that was three years older than the one he'd previously claimed to be. He said it matter-of-factly - like all the other things he had said which were essentially confessions, his voice didn't convey any sense of guilt about the situation. I asked him why he'd chosen that moment to tell me that, and he said it was because he thought the date was going pretty well.

He said he was writing a book about what made art good or bad. I said that whether or not we went on more dates, he was required to share his book with me as that I was pretty sure I'd thought about the topic more than him. He seemed to be very bored about the whole thing.

Again, we disagreed about where we wanted to eat. He said he wanted something different and interesting, like a cafe, and I told him I preferred something more traditional, like a diner, or a nice sit down restaurant. I tried to explain that we could lapse into the pretend versions of ourselves but he was not really listening, or could not understand for some reason. We settled on a bar that had two sides, one just for eating, which was good because I’d forgotten to bring my ID.

He wanted to know all about the situation I’d been in the night before. I had lied to him on the phone and told him I was staying with three lesbian girls. He tried to figure out if they were having me stay with them because they wanted to get with me and asked me questions to determine this. When I mentioned that he was not telling me much about himself, he explained that he did not feel like talking about himself because he had just been on a trip and had had to explain to everyone what he had been doing and he was tired of it.
I had just come from a weird sort of date that lasted for about three days but I concealed that fact by changing the facts a little bit - saying I'd been staying with three lesbians.

He seemed to be trying to figure out whether these fictional women had liked my personality, or whether it had been about them trying to get me to sleep with them. I had to make up more and more "facts" and details about the situation to appease his strange hunger for an understanding of what had happened there at that house where I had been staying for the past few days. I don’t think his findings were conclusive. When the meal was finished, he did not pay for my half of it.

When I mentioned that he was not telling me much about himself, he explained also to me that, because he had just come from a trip in which he had to explain a bunch of things about his life to a lot of people and therefore a lot of times, he was not in the mood to talk about himself, and was content to simply listen to me talk about myself. He said this as though my feelings in the situation were very unimportant. I cannot imagine why he expected me to be fine with that, though I waited for a further explanation. Perhaps he considered it an honor for me to get to talk about myself the whole time, however, it wasn't something that was important to me - it was only something that he was interested in.

He didn't pay for my meal. Afterwards he wanted to go to the supermarket. I wanted to walk but he needed to take his truck. I walked and he met me there in his truck. We stayed until the store closed and just as it was closing, he sent me on a mission to get something he needed (I think it was butter, but there was some confusion about whether it should be salted or not) while he got something else he needed. We got back in the car and I suggested different things we could do but he was tired and eventually we just went home and went to sleep in my bed.
We woke up early, and I was still very tired, but felt slightly sick at having shared a bed with him.

but felt slightly uncomfortable at just having shared a bed with someone I did not like in the slightest. In the morning, he told me that he only found girls that were younger than him attractive. Once again, we were sitting side by side on my couch, this time as I watched him swipe through girls on okcupid. He had his preferences set to girls exactly 22 years of age. He commented on each one, saying they were either ugly, or that they seemed like a slut. My roommate overheard him and asked him to explain what he meant.

Next he argued to me that none of my friends actually wanted to be friends with me and instead that they just wanted to get into my pants. I convinced him that they weren’t trying to get into my pants, citing that none of them had ever tried, even given ample opportunity. He changed tacts, and said they were most likely using me for my emotional intelligence - my ability to help them understand themselves better. I didn’t think this was true either, and told him their emotions rarely came up and we mostly made up strange scenarios together, and giggled vaguely about them.

As we talked, we moved naturally out into the sun outside. I finished by saying that I didn't think I had a superior understanding of emotions, and that they seemed more in touch with their emotions at times. Somehow it ended up that I was lying on the grass outside my house looking up at him, as he claimed, moving away from me while shielding his eyes from the sun, that I had basically surrendered the argument to him because I knew he was right. I didn't think that was fair, but I saw now the potential damage to his very fragile ego, were I, inevitably, to prove myself right, so I simply discontinued the argument, and told him that winning an argument against him wasn’t my intention. After all, I was certain I was right, since he didn’t know much about any of the friendships I was referencing.

I told him that I didn't want to make enough points in order to win the argument but rather I was interested in finding out whether he had any interesting reasoning behind what he was saying and he took that to mean that I had given up. I started to explain how that wasn't true but felt frustrated and explained that he seemed to be changing the terms of our argument so we went inside.

We decided to take a walk around the block and he told me that I had looked better in my pictures. We discussed what our plans for the day were and he said he wanted to go to Powell's books and that perhaps I could come with him and help him pick up girls. He described how this would work.

We would arrive together. We would scour the store for prospective women that he would be interested in hitting on and when we found one he would make sure she had seen us together. He explained that the main point of my being with him was to avoid seeming like a predator. Once we had been seen together we would then separate and I would strike up a conversation with her, him in close proximity. At some point he would join the conversation and if it was going well, I should take the cue and let them finish talking so he could take her home. I told him that I didn't want to do it if that was the end goal, and that I was maybe interested in making friends with girls if that was going to be the end result, but that I didn't want to be his wingman, and that the main point of my being there was to prove that he wasn’t a predator, when I could not, in good conscience, support that claim.

We went back to my house and he unwrapped the two large pieces of meat that he'd bought at the supermarket, letting the gamey smell waft through our meatless household, then cooked both of them for himself and left without cleaning the grease from the pan. My roommate was none too pleased when he arrived back home, as I hadn’t noticed this trace of his horrible rudeness in the wake of his departure.
He called me the following Saturday while I was at a party and I simply let it go to voicemail.

dates.name: Gabriel II
dates.dek: A week later, he was in the neighborhood.

spans.t: A week after my first date with Gabriel he hadn’t texted and I figured I’d misunderstood his feelings towards me. I was frantically typing on my computer an essay about dating which almost never happened when he texted saying he was in the neighborhood and wanted to come over if it wasn’t too late. After I took a shower and talked excitedly to my roommate, warning him to pretend I wasn’t interested because I was playing it cool, we met and walked to a park where we drank some beer.

He told me that he always felt sad now, when he hung out with his friends that did hard drugs and he avoided them as much as possible. He told me about the last time he’d hung out with them and described how they talked, saying “no they really talk like that.” I told him I’d been on three dates since we’d last seen each other and he said why didn’t I call or text him after our date?

I said he’d mentioned he thought I was crazy on our last date and and he said “you weren’t that crazy.” I said well also it was usually the boy’s job to do that. He said “Wait, you’re saying this is a boy girl thing?” He seemed genuinely surprised. He said he’d been to a party at Reed and taken Molly and I was jealous.

He told me he liked to invite friends from different groups that didn’t know each other to hang out together and then not say much and see how they interacted. He decided to go to the diner on Powell that’s open all night. He ordered something and then I just watched him eat without saying anything.

He asked if I was upset with him. I don’t remember what he had said but I was a little upset with him however I said I was just not feeling talkative. I had gotten really quite drunk and on our walk home I ended up laying on the ground in the middle of the street.

I said I would just stay there even though I just wanted him to be nice to me and help me up. He was kind of leaning away from me but not actually leaving, telling me I was being annoying. Finally he did and we walked back to my place and lay next to each other at the foot of my bed not touching until he wanted to go to sleep and moved up to the pillow part of the bed but when I didn’t follow him he moved down again to be next to me.

I woke up before him and spooned him while he was still sleeping and took a picture of his back and made it a moment on tinder. He offered to get up but he said he wanted to keep sleeping so I went into the living room and talked to my roommates until it was time to meet our other roommates to move into our new house.

After that he developed a strange habit of texting me once a month making it seem like he wanted to hang out and then fading away. I ran into him at the bus stop outside the library in Belmont and we had a very amicable conversation and I told him about my website and that I’d quit dating and he said he’d just come back from a trip to California with his friend and of course we made plans to hang out but never did.

dates.name: Jacob
dates.dek: He was from Canada.

spans.t: he was from canada When I was sad, bored, in the kitchen and wondering blahdy blah what I shud do but omg no that cute boy from tinder wants to see me? I made it seem like I wasn’t concerned and but then asked him to aww a barbecue at the house next door. And I remembered his funny response to whatever I had up at the time.

I didn’t realize he was actually coming; I thought I hadn’t replied enough that he’d forgotten about me. I was talking to Alpha in the kitchen, explaining something on our white board. But then meeting him commanded my attention for the next day and a quarter. I went outside and he was on a skateboard?!

And he’d broken ribs to come meet me is what I interpreted him as saying. I concerned myself with the fact that my casual idea had meant an actual other person having to drive (skateboard) miles and miles in the burning sun and bitter snowy cold. We met outside in the dark and so we couldn’t see each other at first.

I took him the wrong way for a while because I’d been holed up in the kitchen and wanted to walk. All of a sudden we were just like excited and fun having and cute and laughing and having hilarious fun but what the hell the minute after we met but already making jokes. I couldn’t think that a cutesy boy like him would want to come meet me.

He was small but he had the cutest mouth and nose and eyes like a doll and this like huge strip of crowny brown hair that was covering his face. I started thinking about Canada. And that never happens to me. I remember us walking sweet breezy in the moonlight ooh god a sweet face of that tree oh can you count the things that are good about this?

Right away I noticed there was something serious about his playfulness, a hidden undercurrent of a point he was making that I hate and couldn’t take but it was all so sweetly covered in ridiculousness and manners. I brought him over though and alpha was there coming on his conveyor belt to the kitchen to the stairs.

I stood under the bright hostile lights of my kitchen, feeling simultaneously worried he would be disappointed with his date if he’d expected to be attracted to me and caught in this lime light spotlight of the perfect girl that you have to meet because she is so interesting and cool and now she is lightly shifting her weight to feel light to herself, balancing on the cabinet behind her to feel free and to imbue the appropriate amount of displayed discomfort that is appropriate for a first date and meeting in your kitchen that you are supposed to display on a hashtag first date.

It forced me immediately into an “I’m a player” sense of being which I know I will fit into on any tinder occasion. I adopted my “I’m slightly cooler and better than you” proposal accidentally which he seemed to embrace and even take seriously or something; maybe I’m completely wrong. \{In his weds, he kept climbing up to things and the top of the cute narrow mountain he’d created was so narrow it was just a sliver sloping sideways.\} I wanted to hold his hand but I put my hand next to his and then compulsively linked arms with him.

He said like “if we want to do this right we might as well…” So then we held hands the whole way there and it was so nice. Even when we encountered a pole which caused us to unlink, we unanimously voted silently to relink afterwards, and it became almost like an unspoken ritual. We laughed about physics, we laughed about other stuff, we interspersed it with swift observations about rule based systems.

We got lost or something and I brought up that I always got lost and that I was bad at directions and also other logical mental processes like math or no now I remember I told him about dropping out of school and explained it as that I just “couldn’t” do the work cause I like that story, I like telling it to people cause the facts all fit.

He tried to make me feel better by saying that physics is hard. I was shocked that I still had to play that game “I’m stupid” when we’d already bonded over such a range of topics. He was surprised when I mentioned my major was neuroscience. We went to the first bar and went inside and it felt bad and like we were about to have to force conversation or something so we left.

I noticed that from the time that we sat on the wooden bench at pizza on Ainsworth I almost said completely nothing save for when I picked up a phone call. People kept calling me twice that day which means I have to answer in case it’s important. He told me though about being treated at a facility for like seven months.

When he started talking about it he seemed like a smaller boy, telling me about his day at school that had been scary and confusing and he’d come away with a somewhat skewed perception as he was a kid and it helped him to understand things better if they made sense. While he was talking I felt compelled to relate with my own experiences, but I wanted to let him tell me his experience in that way when someone knows they’re telling you something strange that you won’t quite relate to at first.

I wanted him to have the pleasure of knowing he was introducing me to something I had not experienced, because, though I had experienced all the parts that were new to both of us, I still had not had his same experience. I could live vicariously through him, and take myself back to a time when I did not know the horrors of what happened in places such as he spoke of.

He seemed at times to be intellectually smitten with me and at the same time standoffish a little and not trying to suggest that we should kiss more or hold hands more. He kept saying how smitten he was. He kept noting my hilarity and tendency to have ridiculous interesting things to say. He kept saying that together we were having the most interesting conversation anyone had ever had.

I felt uncomfortable that I had told him about my dates not being interested in what I had to say and the swift monopolization of our conversation and also ached to say something but it was against the rules you know? I slipped up and blurted a barrage of blah blah blah about my other dates wondering if I seemed worrisomely detached.

I was, despite myself, interested in the fact that he seemed to be well renowned as a beer connoisseur. I felt like I was learning about a foreign country when he talked about his position. I was in a beautiful space talking to him and he held me aloft with his constant reminders that we were having a good time.

I felt myself judging him in his own eyes which I was but not for the things he thought I was I think. He paid for my drinks and we put our arms around each other on the walk home. At first I wanted to go meet his friends at the hostel downtown because it seemed like an interesting experience.

Then when he was actually trying to plan this I wondered if his initial enthusiasm had turned to boredom or something. The idea was disposed of after a phone call to his hostel mate and we settled on the couch and he explained something to me with an unfitting amount of encouragement on my part and perhaps a tinge of self-awareness about displaying my ability to comprehend complicated things quickly.

On our upstairs part of the night I was on my way downstairs when he made a joke about my undressing which catalyzed taking off my own overalls (I think they were the slutty black ones). It felt as awkward as I thought it would and I slipped myself underneath a blanket. There was some strange closeness like we were really actually close to being actual friends that I felt under the covers.

I watched his head move as he told me about this girl he’d known. He told me all about this girl he’d dated. They’d had chemistry so much chemistry they’d seriously met on chat roulette blah blah blah a pretend pregnancy and then a suicide attempt I didn’t like her from the story but felt bad for the pain she must have suffered and as one of the things that never gets mentioned I wonder why that wasn’t a topic of our conversation.

I couldn’t quite picture why he’d choose to be in such a relationship. He hadn’t presented himself as un-selfconfident and he certainly wasn’t unattractive and he was smart like really wholy smart. His banter was and like did keep going and he did actually know everything that I was saying. Every time I felt that we were about to descend into common philosophical misrepresented platitudes it became cutesy and funny.

There were a few instances of him reflecting on the various ways that words can mean things that almost pissed me off to no end however I was not in the mood for that (for being pissed off). Oh what a strange moment when he suggested that I take medication for my “mental illness.” I settled for believing that once one had discussed with themselves the weighty reasons for weighing themselves down with reasons, their reasons became like a physical object and trying to push them through conversation was inappropriate.

It was unpleasant, it felt like other times, I decided that the fact that he wasn’t wearing a shirt and was in my bed (was he wearing a shirt? It’s unclear now) was reason enough to dismiss the salty charges from my brain with the reasoning I mentioned formed. It didn’t matter. It dissolved into more conversation an we solved it later when he pretended he’d been kidding.

Then it was about this really beautiful tall girl who he knew and actually enjoyed having sex with which I can imagine I would too. I could picture her over him well I tried to because that’s what I was studying that day and his disinterest in sex was interesting to me and this was the counter example so I pictured it.

In the middle of the night, one of my dates called me for the second time so I answered and talked to him in the bathroom for a good half an hour, wondering how Jacob might have cared about that. I slipped back into bed beside him and we resumed cuddling, an easy friendliness between us.

I liked when he said that his friend had changed his pictures that day to ones that he felt were much less good and I agreed. We spent most of the time talking about the strangeness of him not really being interested in having sex with girls. I recall he told me when he met me that he wasn’t interested in tinder to hook up with people blah who says that, what boy?
Or was he saying that cuz he was scared of me trying to hook up with him: my worst fear?
