There were a few instances of him reflecting on the various ways that words can mean things that almost pissed me off to no end however I was not in the mood for that (for being pissed off).

Oh what a strange moment when he suggested that I take medication for my "mental illness." I settled for believing that once one had discussed with themselves the weighty reasons for weighing themselves down with reasons, their reasons became like a physical object and trying to push them through conversation was inappropriate. It was unpleasant, it felt like other times, I decided that the fact that he wasn't wearing a shirt and was in my bed (was he wearing a shirt? It's unclear now) was reason enough to dismiss the salty charges from my brain with the reasoning I mentioned formed. It didn't matter. It dissolved into more conversation an we solved it later when he pretended he'd been kidding.

Then it was about this really beautiful tall girl who he knew and actually enjoyed having sex with which I can imagine I would too. I could picture her over him well I tried to because that's what I was studying that day and his disinterest in sex was interesting to me and this was the counter example so I pictured it.

In the middle of the night, one of my dates called me for the second time so I answered and talked to him in the bathroom for a good half an hour, wondering how Jacob might have cared about that. I slipped back into bed beside him and we resumed cuddling, an easy friendliness between us.
I liked when he said that his friend had changed his pictures that day to ones that he felt were much less good and I agreed.

We spent most of the time talking about the strangeness of him not really being interested in having sex with girls. I recall he told me when he met me that he wasn't interested in tinder to hook up with people blah who says that, what boy? Or was he saying that cuz he was scared of me trying to hook up with him: my worst fear?

dates.name: Andrew
dates.dek: A Friday night that started as a photo shoot.

spans.t: It was quite late and I’d been thinking of going out all day, afterall, it was a Friday. Instead I was on the bench in the kitchen playing with my tinder account. Alpha came home at around 10 and we suddenly got into a photo shoot (I was wearing my black overalls and my orange shirt).

I posed in front of the oven, then we moved to the living room for different lighting, then I started taking pictures of him. After we finished, he went upstairs and I left our house, ostensibly to get beer from the 711 which I did, I bought a pack of Total Domination and got into a “conversation” with this guy who was old and attractive and right off the bat told me it was great that I was talking to him and about how people generally considered him a monster and I noticed that he was visibly shaking, he seemed very wired and I even asked him if he was on adderall or something despite the fact that I hate when people ask whether I’m on drugs.

He told me a story after I asked him where he was going, about his friend who he was on the way back from, and how his daughter, while everyone else considered him a monster, had gone right up to him and talked to him and that naturally he’d become friends with the mother and father after a successful interaction such as that.

He told me that I was beautiful, in saying that girls like me never talked to him. I felt conflicted between wanting to end the interaction and wanting to continue it but after it was over I impulsively reached for a reeses pieces and a slurpee. Besides my beer, I ended up buying a mango smoothie for Alpha which was the original mission, plus an ice cream snickers bar which I opened inside of the 711 and proceeded to eat a third of, and then toss into my back pack despite the fact that ice cream has been known to melt.

I made my way from there to Alberta, no particular plan in mind, perhaps simply enjoying having left the house finally. But there are lots of bars on Alberta street and I knew one might hold something fun. I had a large case of beer and certainly couldn’t bring it into any bars, nor was I enjoying carting it around, nor the potential future of carting it around anymore.

I kept changing the way I was carrying it, I’m pretty sure I’d stuffed it into my backpack in case carrying beer was illegal, I couldn’t remember and wasn’t wearing the backpack but holding it out in front of me in different positions. I hightailed it to the Radio Room which is a bar that I like, after carefully hiding the paper bag full of beer behind a drain pipe in front of a yellow building, not fully sure what I intended to do with it after that, noting, though, that the building was yellow so that I could find it if I needed to.

I sat down at the bar at the radio room and ordered a beer and was mind-numbingly pleased with the sensation of alcohol entering my body, I’m pretty sure it was a red beer, as my taste was getting progressively lighter since moving to Portland. After a few moments, a big guy with frizzy brown hair and a band around his forehead sat next to me and started talking to the bartender about how much people had to tip if they forgot their cards at the bar (never closed out).

He seemed to think everyone should tip a lot more — like 20%. He turned to me and asked what I thought. I don’t remember what I said. I’m not fully in favor of tipping a lot, and that is mostly because I ration my money very carefully. He told me that recently he’d been working on his speed reading techniques.

We had a speed reading contest of To Kill a Mockingbird — the sparknotes summary version — of which I set the rules for. After we finished it was unclear how the winner was to be decided. I had a very difficult time staying focused on the material despite my previous confidence about being able to absorb a lot of information quickly and wondered about the relevance of the bar being so loud.

We haphazardly explained what we could remember reading in the book and moved onto a summary of a book by Faulker which was long and ridiculous and I actually remember had something to do with people that have kids and then other people that have more kids and some sort of misunderstanding. I read a lot more of that book than the other one and was somewhat proud to have remembered some of it or even to have comprehended the summary as I was reading it.

After a while we talked about other stuff; I told him I blogged about stuff he said that he was the bassist in a band, and that he was planning to play a show in Eugene the next day. At some point a red-haired boy came up to him and told him that he and some girl were about to leave and my new friend decided he’d stay with me.

He begged me to let him walk me home, promising not to try anything sexual and I didn’t mind at all and pretended like it wasn’t completely ridiculous, him begging me to do this, as though I wasn’t already trying to engineer the situation according to the potential of a similar outcome. Either way, we got hopelessly lost on the way home and I remember collapsing on someone’s grass at some point, (and apparently not remembering to take my backpack with me because I couldn’t find it the next morning and had to pick it up from a nice old couple, who told me I should have a passcode, even though it was precisely the lack of a passcode that had let them contact me, in the first place) and he sitting next to me I think and making out for a moment on the wet grass.

We got to my house, I had to have Alpha let us in which he did and then went straight back to bed. We went upstairs and fell asleep in my bed and in the morning he had to get up early and had to go to Eugene and was awakened by one of his band mates calling him and saying that they had to catch the train so he left.

dates.name: Gabriel B
dates.dek: He growled at me.

spans.t: he growled at me He said he did not want to go my room because he did not want to have sex with me He said that me taking a shower meant I had persuaded him to have sex with me He bought me sour patch kids He tried to help a homeless guy in front of the mini mart He said I was shorter than my pictures He opened his beer in the car while he was driving He left the beer bottles at my house He growled at me when we were having sex He told me about recovering from being a heroin addict We’d been messaging for a while and had almost met up once but he told me he was “too broke.”

His first message had been something like “fiddly-Doo” which I liked (but found out later it was actually a quote from a movie I’d never seen). The day before I planned to have my Andrew Party Alpha had taken me shopping. First to get a piñata and then to Safeway to get beer and taco things.

Gabriel messaged me and we decided to meet at the Bye and Bye Bar on Alberta. I walked there from my house and didn’t notice that I had dropped my wallet on the way so when I got there before him I couldn’t get in because I didn’t have my ID. When he met me, I was sitting at a picnic table right next to the entrance and had to stand up and practically shout his name to get his attention because he was about to walk in without seeing me.

I told him my predicament and he said we could go look for it. I got sort of hopeless that we would find it. We walked a little bit up the street to see if it was there and then turned around to see if it was the other way. I told him I wanted to give up.

I’m not sure what we discussed on that walk all I remember is that it was hard to make conversation wit him because he wasn’t very talkative and that at some point he told me I was shorter than I’d looked in my pictures which offended me to be honest. We decided to get beer from a store and he bought a six pack of Lagunitas and I said I wanted sour patch kids also so he got them and seemed to be talking to the guy who was asking for money outside the gas station for a while and then gave him something.

He started drinking even though we were in the car; he opened a beer for both of us with his car keys, or his lighter or something. And we drove back to my house except we drove around for a little while because I didn’t tell him when to turn. He told me he’d had problems with drugs at some point in his life and that he’d quit.

At my house I showed him around and he thought it was really cool. He didn’t seem to want to go with me to my room but he did and then he said something about how he wasn’t gonna let me coerce him into having sex with him. We left and went back outside to look for my wallet and I found it a few blocks from my house and was quite happy.

He drove us then to a bar I’d never been to before on Alberta and he bought us each a beer and a shot and things seemed to be going well but then we didn’t really have anything to talk about. He told me more about the problems with drugs he’d experienced. At one point he said it was too bad he had work the next day, or he would have driven us both to a beach that was about two hours away.

I’ve got to say I was surprised by this statement, thinking someone would want to commit to a short trip with someone they’d just met, and might be quite annoying. I didn’t say anything because I couldn’t quite believe it. And perhaps it was only something someone would say in passing, anyway.

dates.name: Adam
dates.dek: The ol’ switcheroo.

spans.t: the ol’ switcheroo My Date with Adam When we were in the house, I really couldn’t take it. I made some jokes at first, as I was putting all my clothes on, after I invited him inside and did nothing to relieve the tension that came from the boundary of my house being dismantled. I went straight back to the desk with the computer wondering if maybe I could just continue writing.

When he was at the door, through the hole in the wood, I could see that he was attractive. His dark brown hair was in front of his face, and he was tall. The whole house seeming like gleaming candy. I laced up my shoes and tossed my jacket on and my backpack over my shoulder and moved around the beautiful wooden floors like I was hot shit.

I told him about my Andrew party as I zipped my jacket. I told him about the phone that only calls Big Bird in the kitchen. He was standing in front of the kitchen table, waiting for me to get all of my stuff and I moved closer to him and he moved away and I moved away.

He hovered next to the kitchen table, almost interacting with the side of the wood and I came over to him and almost to him and almost touched him. He moved away from me though and I moved away too. We met at Beulahland. No we didn’t. He picked me up at my house. My house seeming purple and pink, me bending forward to attach my laces to themselves to each other and to seem like I was occupied and busy – to seem like there was something I was going to do – I was a king masquerading as a queen.

Everything was compiled in the rim of a pair of see-through glasses. Through the royal threshold that led between the dining room and the kitchen I moved, being flippant and adding some politeness as an afterthought. He went with me between the rooms and went with me between the jokes I was making, following at a reasonable distance.

He hovered at the edge of the wooden kitchen table and I came to stand next to him and almost touch him. He flicked himself away to stand slightly to the left so my experiment to see whether I could initiate a physical connection without the preamble of the date had failed. As I made my way around that little space of the kitchen, I began to feel faint.

I overwhelmingly didn’t want to pretend, or make small talk and I wondered if I could simply refuse. I found myself standing on the step above him and was at about his height. I decided to move my head the two inches it would take to reach his. But I didn’t do it. Instead the date went on and he moved back into the kitchen and said resignedly that we should just go to the bar that he had been at.

He led the way outside to his car which was white and notably not falling apart. It seemed like a sports car but I don’t know anything about sports cars. There was something about the front engine that screamed class and that it had taken a little bit of money to buy it. We went inside the car and I note that he had a watch on his wrist and therefore was not exactly a hipster.

It also had hair; so he felt like a man. I was at my desk in the computer room when their appeared a face with brown hair on top of it in the pane of glass that is part of the door, casually. I figured that he was waiting for me to come get him for the date that we’d arranged beforehand so I walked away from my silver computer to open the door for him even though I was still working on the metaphysical theory I’d been engrossed in before this young man came to my house in the middle of the day for what seemed like no particular reason except that there existed a thread of digital communication which had made it occur.

He told me about his job, at evergreen. We got out of the car, we went into the restaurant. I pulled out my wallet to pay for my beer. He said that he had too much money and needed to know what to spend it on. I let him pay for my drink and the drinks turned black then as soon as we got them because they were mine because I hadn’t paid for them.

It wasn’t that he had it was that I hadn’t and so they were black and so things were good. He brought us tall brown bottles of beer that had a red label and white inside of that. We drank them. Pretty fast. I lolled at the table, turning brown – the same color as the dark side of the beer bottles that rolled down from the liquid inside of them.

It seemed unlikely to do anything and while he was in the bathroom I pulled out white note cards that I was in the habit of bringing with me. And we drew ideas for things that we could do that day. We both had a card that said “tell something horrible that happened to you” and his had the addendum that it should not be too terrible.

He said it was because he didn’t want us to start talking about our dead parents. I told him about the night before where I had been stumbling around drunk by myself for literally the entire night. And I’d lost my backpack. Somehow I doubted he’d ever been involved in something so silly, and so stupid, but he told me one night he’d fallen asleep on some grass somewhere outside a bar, woken up after it was closed, and walked to his house and got there when the buses started running.

He said he always sometimes went to sleep in the day as the buses would rumble up outside his window every 20 minutes. He would sometimes scream at them. The cards turning white that we were playing on – the two tinges – the flashes of the perked up white that is to come. He leaves to get us another beer.

The guy at the table in front of us looks at me “It sounds like you guys are having a very interesting conversation. Is it a first date?” I reply yes. When he returned, we began speaking about art. A common interest, it seemed. He began explaining his artistic process involved creating a digital work, and then printing out the picture, but then deleting the digital file.

I understood that this meant that while his work had most of the qualities of being digital, it wasn’t automatically reproducible, and I wondered if this made it more rare for him. In spite of myself, I was impressed with his courage to delete a digital file, and my mind thought of all sorts of alternatives (saving it on a usb, just telling people it was deleted), before I remembered this was the exact point of the work.

I wanted him to know that I knew what he was explaining, without him having to even say it. Stunned that he was still explaining what I already knew I tried to magically ooze myself between his words like bubble syrup explaining that I could say the same thing that he was saying to me to him.

“You see? You get it?” Yes I saw, yes I got it. No oozing allowed. Dear Adam I’m sorry, this is true, this is just what happened. I took a picture of the four bottles of beer laid out in front of me like tracks, explaining things to me through their silence and the longing that was produced by the spaces between them.

I could feel myself slipping, lying down on the fuzzy carpet that was between us, just falling into the ball pit, letting myself get shot at the shooting range, collapsing. I couldn’t explain the silences like I usually could, I let them get to me. Finally we discovered our mutual interest in the movie Donnie Darko, and under the pretense of watching it, returned to his room where we soon found it was impossible.

Instead we were able to find something else to entertain ourselves. The light was growing dim through the large window in his immaculate space, the biggest room in the house, and I lay face down against his pillows, tired from my lack of sleep and he simply lifted my skirt. I might have minded, but he wouldn’t have known, but I didn’t.

Afterwards we made our way into his but instead of getting out as he did, reaching for a white towel hung from the wall, unready for the experience to be over, and still maybe so so tired, I closed my eyes and lay back against the wall of the tub. He came through the space in the curtains and started kissing me and his hands came through as well, through the space the curtains made.

What had just been began again, and He stumbled up from the bed. “Let’s do something. Let’s go get a drink.” Was there a drink on the dresser, or somewhere? I was so tired, it was hard to get out of bed. I was simply delighted that he hadn’t somehow fallen for me and wanted to spend the night sleeping all cuddly and he didn’t already want to dismiss me.

He wanted still to get to know me and we could transition back into the dating phase and that was right, since we’d only been hanging out for a few hours. we got up to go to the bar. We went to Swift. We talked to his roommate briefly before we left and Adam talked to him about meeting us there.

Swift was a warm bar, and all the colors were in oranges. There were lots of people lolling around everywhere, starting to do things with each other, all sorts of things. I walked into the bar with Adam, and Adam told me to stand by our table so I could save it for us. Perhaps because I’d offered to pay for my drink at the beginning of the date, he seemed then willing to buy all sorts of other things for me, not least of all was the burger, the cocaine, the coffee, and some more drinks. they talked about going skiing on mount hood.

I sort of leaned my head down on Adam a little bit, but just for a second because he didn’t reciprocate at all, didn’t grab my head and pull it towards him. And then in the morning, we had great sex again. Even, when he got up to put the condom on, I didn’t want to let go of his hand because I like having sex with him, and I felt connected to him, he reached up to where the dresser was, and the fucked up sun was coming in through the window and Iin my stupo They wanted to pay for me.

They wanted to buy me cocaine. They wanted to sit next to me and talk about the impending excitement of buying cocaine with me and for me. The girl at the table next to us started laughing listening to our conversation. I asked them what skiing meant, trying to muster up enough mental energy to become excited and interested in potentially going to Mt.

Hood right then and sliding down some icy slopes so I could think of a strategy to get them to invite me. It hurt my feelings that they didn’t seem planning to invite me. The man at the table next to us went away from his girl. She started chuckling . - \\ There was a medium sized plastic bag and shuffled towards the bottom in a loose heap was this weird white powder, a tiny bit pinkish I think.

It was all jumbly and manic inside the bag, and wasn’t ground up very well it seemed. They started pouring small amounts onto the table and using a card to crush them up. Adam offered bits to me. I asked if he knew Hennessey Youngman. He said he was friends with him on facebook. I couldn’t resist but make fun of him and to say “Ohh you’re friends with him on facebook” to which he reacted like I’d struck him a little bit.

I asked if he knew Die Antwoord. We spent most of the night watching these weird videos of South African kids on their front lawns doing strange sexual dances and talking about whether it was meant to be sexual at all. I was like a worm and was inching towards the beginning of the couch.

When I fell asleep on the couch, they left and went to buy the cocaine. I was curious what had happened when I fell asleep. one of them said “Cocaine. ayyyyne.” (I asked Alex the next day. He told me that they’d gone to a strange building and he’d stayed in the car and Adam had gone into the strange van of his drug dealer.

He said that he’d thought that maybe Adam would die during the time that he was in there. I didn’t believe that he’d thought that, or it seemed strange that he would use that as an opportunity to contemplate death of all things, and not the strangeness of the situation in general. I wondered if he had really perceived a threat or it seemed childish to think that, to have that thought while Adam was in the other car.

Adam told me that one time the same drug dealer had asked him if he could drive him somewhere and it had turned into a long list of errands that Adam had to deal with — about two hours…this added into a pattern that was developing of Adam being somewhat of a pushover or something, or making himself available to being somewhat abused by people.

Other things that were added to that category were the girl he’d talked about who he hadn’t described as seeming to care about him that much but had seemed to rope him into different things. Also him paying for everything for me — all the cocaine. I had tried not to take too much advantage of him.

And also being very very nice — offering to drive his roommate to work, grabbing the coffee lid for me, holding the door open whenever we went anywhere, apologizing for not having me sit in the front. Alex put out a different pattern. I was a little aware of him manipulating his patterns and telling me certain things.

I was well aware of myself manipulating my patterns or certainly seeming to manipulate or potentially manipulate my patterns in regards to recounting my previous experience in dating. He asked me to tell him a question and I wanted him to have the experience of feeling uncomfortably questioned beyond what he felt comfortable with because he obviously desired that experience and I knew how sacred it was to be made to tell something that you didn’t necessarily want to or to be invited to share more than could be accounted for by the situation just because you were invited to.

The same thrill of truth or dare — the invitation where the reward far exceeds the vulnerability it takes to make the invitation.) It was that or spend the night at my new “life-long friend” that I’d met on Craigslist that day, who wanted me to move into the closet-sized, window-less room upstairs almost as much as he wanted to lecture me on how being a vegan wasn’t really a choice as much as a lifestyle.

I arranged to meet my date at a stand up comedy club in downtown after notifying him that I would need to spend the night at his house. I took the bus there and texted lots of people while I was on it, including my dad I think. I arrived and he was sitting near the entrance in a tall canvas chair and neglected to interact with me besides waving me over.

His awkwardness and the fact that he was not very attractive made me disappointed in myself. I texted people more during the show, namely my mom. Which guy? The one who’d read all of his jokes out of a lined notebook he’d set on the stool next to him. Which ones had been funny (none), and how better to present them, down to microscopic details like word choice. in which a performer singled us out for not laughing and I defended a girl whose birthday it was after after her set the MC made a joke about liking the fact that girls don’t enjoy blow jobs.

One disappointingly hellish stand-up comedy show later and we were outside analyzing, with future Louis CK himself, microscopic details of his own jokes. It was my fault as I had initiated the interaction by asking him to “explain” his last joke which hadn’t made sense to myself or anyone in the audience. He mistook my plea which was really a jab as a request from an adoring fan, and explained, to my date but not to me, this joke plus numerous other ones that we didn’t ask for.

If there’s ever a time I regret not punching someone in the face…but I digress. Myself, this moron, my disappointingly unattractive OkCupid date, and my disappointingly unattractive okcupid date’s roommate Chris, who I mistakenly called Brian a little over three times went outside to watch as he “did a quick run down,” of the microscopic details of every joke he had told, pilfering the air space with the squeaks from the skateboard he was allowing to lifelessly move beneath him.

I went inside to use the bathroom and while peeing, thought up an excellent joke to add to the mix. It goes: “If I had a quarter for every time people ignored me at the end of a comedy show, then I would probably patent the technology that enables me to receive money every time an arbitrary event occurs and make a living wage off of that.”

Alex the up-and-coming soon-to-be-very-famous monotone comic gave me a pity laugh, then told me it was because he didn’t want it to be awkward and also he wanted to encourage nubes. I thought of another joke and told it to them, this one even more blatantly about being ignored and explained both of them to my date sort of quietly.

After this my date, who got it, and I, started to get along pretty well and made lots of jokes together on our way to the car together, and in the car together, in which I sat in the back seat so that his roommate, fat, actually-Brian Chris could sit in the front. His house was extremely far away and I passed the spot where Thomas and I had met on the side of the road that one night next to the mini mart and the bus stop.

When we arrived at his house, two more unattractive nerdy boys emerged from the woodwork — I mean came out of the kitchen. One was small and Indian, the other had a ginger afro and lots of acne. They were gearing up to play Mario Kart together on the one piece of furniture in their house, which was a large purple couch opposite the TV.

There was absolutely nothing on the walls, and the whole house smelled like pizza. I joked that they had slightly too much furniture to my date who was standing near the doorway still (I had walked to the fold out table to put my yellow legal pad down and other stuff) except he didn’t understand what I was saying and was confused and said that he didn’t think there was too much furniture, in fact he didn’t think there was much furniture at all.

I had to explain it to him. I wrote down some thoughts I’d been thinking while he talked to his roommates sorta, and then he offered me a thermos which it turned out contained a two week old vodka cranberry that tasted like vinegar because vinegar is what you get when a beverage is left sitting long enough to ferment.

He told me the story of how he’d “lost” his drink, and then it had turned up again about three days — no maybe more like a week — later, and then he’d put it into the thermos I now held in my faintly quivering hand. I excused myself to try and vomit and he laughed nervously, saying he didn’t think alcohol could go bad.

Before I had tasted it, I searched the entire kitchen for some sort of drinking apparatus other than the thermos, more formally known as a cup. There were none, the last thing on the shelf you might consider a mini-cup (also known as a shot glass), which I poured a small amount of while he was in the other room with his friends doing something, and filled it and drank some and left the tiny glass near the sink since I wasn’t going to drink the rest of it.

I asked him what it was and he said “vodka cranberry” and I said there might be vinegar in it to which he replied that he didn’t think so. He wanted to show me his basement where he and his roommates put on a weekly podcast show so I went down with him and we looked at all the lego things he had there and I asked if I could play the drums and he said it was fine and that one of the advantages of living so far away from everything was that it was permissable to make loud noises even in the middle of the night so I gave the drums a few loud thwacks and then turned away from them and put the drumsticks back, resting on one of the round platforms.

We went back upstairs after I made fun of him for offering me an expired drink and he refused to believe that there could actually be vinegar in it and said it tasted fine. He led me into his bedroom but I lingered outside, asking awkwardly what he did for work so that he was forced to pose half-leaning on the side of the refrigerator.

He worked at Subway, he said, which was why he only had eleven dollars in his wallet and couldn’t afford to take me anywhere where the spending of money was encouraged and/or required. There was no escape so I entered his room gingerly sitting as far from him as possible on the bed while he inched toward me, oblivious to my subtle defensive moves like placing my feet out in front of me so he couldn’t get any closer without breaking the threshold of my lap.He went into his room and implied that I should come in too but I stayed outside in the hallway and we stayed there, him standing against the refrigerator and me standing against the wall.

He asked me what I did for a living after I told him it wasn’t cool that he worked at Subway because no one likes Subway and he agreed and I said that it was even less cool that I didn’t have a job at all. He invited me into his room and I asked if perhaps we might go to a bar and he said that he didn’t have any money to spend at a bar — that he had exactly 11 dollars and that needed to last him till payday.

I forget his answer.Finally we went into his room and sat on his bed next to each other talking. It was pleasant and we had figured out our senses of humor and were bantering joyfully.

We discussed possibly doing a double stand up comedy act, because I told him that he was funnier than his friend and for that matter all the people that had been on stage. dates.dek: I called his name twice and he didn’t turn around.

spans.t: I saw the back of Gabriel’s head when I went to the Hot Cake House and called “Gabriel” twice but he didn’t turn around. So I went to his table where he was standing looking around being confused and tapped him twice on the forearm and when he turned around I started giggling in his face, except I was just a tiny bit below him, but just a tiny bit and babbling at him.

He hasn’t really talked so I say “what are you doing?” and he says “Oh, I just spilled beer on myself” and I see that there is a can of Tecate hanging out next to the one table leg and that, yeah, his butt is kinda wet. But he’s not really doing anything, he’s turning slightly in a few directions and just looking very confused.

So after I said whatever I said, which I don’t remember, I went back to my seat with the other guy. “No, we have to go back, I want to punch him in the face.” I wasn’t intending at all to punch him in the face, but I thought that might be interesting enough for him to want to go back.

So we went back and I went to the bathroom. I spent most of the time in the bathroom trying to decide what clothes to wear on my way back, and staring into the mirror, and imagining myself walking past his table and not saying anything. But when I came back they weren’t at their table anymore, they were outside doing stuff like smoking idk and I walked past them and they said something and I turned around and said “Just going to my car with my boyfriend…” and he said “You got a car?” incredulously, and I said: “Well, I mean, my boyfriend has it, so basically,” and then I started to walk away to the car, pretty much just imagining how my butt must look wearing the white silky dress, and how it looked in those pants too.

And then he went: “Yeh. Yeh. Yeh.” like he was maybe choking, it wasn’t clear, and I turned back once, to make sure he was ok, but then I kept going and got into the car and we drove away. I tried to talk about other stuff, but mostly just went: “yeah, that wen’t pretty well, huh, like that couldn’t have gone better, could it have?”
